## Abstract


For the first time in the history of physics, thermodynamics is derived as a chain of formal theorems descending from a single physical principle—the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$—which states that the fourth dimension is expanding at the velocity of light in a spherically symmetric manner from every spacetime event. General relativity and quantum mechanics have each been the subject of multiple foundational-derivation programs over the past century. Each sector has had a *crowded* foundational-principle literature. And in the same 1932 volume in which he codified the Hilbert-space axiomatization, von Neumann articulated the structural recognition that orthodox thermodynamics has ignored for ninety-four years: *"the principle of continuity ('natura non facit saltus'), prevailing in the macroscopic world, is merely simulated by an averaging process in a world which in truth is discontinuous by its very nature ... the leveling law of large numbers completely obscures the real nature of the individual processes"* [vonNeumann1932]. Von Neumann's recognition — that classical thermodynamics is the leveled-out averaged signature of quantum-mechanical elementary processes — is the structural anticipation, ninety-four years in advance, of the foundational identification made rigorous in the present paper: the elementary processes are Compton-coupled $x_4$-expansion ticks at every event (Theorem 4); the averaging is the Lindeberg-Lévy CLT applied to the matter-tier ensemble (Theorem 9); the leveling is the diffusion that supplies both the Second Law and the Navier-Stokes viscous smoothing. Von Neumann saw the structural identity; the McGucken Principle supplies the missing mechanism.

**Thermodynamics has had no formal derivation from foundational physical principles.** Since Boltzmann's 1877 statistical retreat—which abandoned the H-theorem's foundational ambition in favor of a probabilistic reading after Loschmidt's 1876 reversibility objection—there has been no structural derivation program for thermodynamics from a deeper physical principle at all. The Boltzmann–Gibbs framework supplies the calculational machinery; the Maximum-Entropy approach of Jaynes 1957 reformulates it epistemically; the Past Hypothesis (Albert, Loewer, Carroll) reinterprets the cosmological boundary condition; Jacobson 1995 and Verlinde 2010 extend it into spacetime physics. Einstein's 1949 admission that thermodynamics is a "theory of principle" whose reduction to mechanics has not been completed is the honest reflection of this absence: 150 years after Loschmidt, the foundational-derivation question for thermodynamics had remained open.

The historical first established by the present paper is therefore stronger than the corresponding firsts in the GR and QM sectors: the gravity and QM chain papers are *firsts among many programs*; the present thermodynamic chain paper is a *first among none*. ## Introduction


> *"A theory is the more impressive the greater is the simplicity of its premises, the more different are the kinds of things it relates and the more extended the range of its applicability. Therefore the deep impression which classical thermodynamics made upon me. It is the only physical theory of universal content which I am convinced will never be overthrown, within the framework of applicability of its basic concepts."*  
>   — Albert Einstein, *Autobiographical Notes*, 1949


> *"A physical theory can be satisfactory only if its structures are composed of elementary foundations. The theory of relativity is ultimately as little satisfactory as, for example, classical thermodynamics was before Boltzmann had interpreted the entropy as probability."*  
>   — Albert Einstein


### Einstein's 1949 Admission and the Three Gaps


In his 1949 autobiographical notes Einstein wrote that classical thermodynamics "is the only physical theory of universal content which I am convinced will never be overthrown, within the framework of applicability of its basic concepts." This sentence is often quoted as a tribute. It is better read as a confession.

Einstein had spent 1902–1904 deriving statistical mechanics independently of Gibbs, and his 1905 Brownian motion paper was the decisive empirical vindication of the molecular-kinetic hypothesis. Yet by 1949 he called thermodynamics a *theory of principle*—explicitly contrasted with *constructive theories* built from hypothesized microscopic models. The implication is that thermodynamics survives because it has not been successfully reduced to mechanics, not because the reduction has been completed.

Three structural gaps prevent the reduction:


- ****(T1)**** **The probability-measure problem.** Boltzmann and Gibbs postulate the uniform Liouville measure on phase space and the principle of equal a priori probabilities; these are postulates, with Liouville's theorem (1838) providing preservation given the choice but not justification for the choice.
- ****(T2)**** **The ergodicity problem.** Ergodicity is assumed despite KAM theory (Kolmogorov 1954, Arnold 1963, Moser 1962) demonstrating that generic Hamiltonian perturbations preserve a positive-measure set of invariant tori, so the ergodic hypothesis is not merely unproven but for typical physical systems demonstrably *false*.
- ****(T3)**** **The arrow-of-time problem.** Loschmidt's 1876 reversibility objection and Zermelo's 1896 recurrence objection remain structurally unresolved; Boltzmann's H-theorem requires the Stosszahlansatz, which smuggles irreversibility into a time-symmetric substrate. The Second Law in the orthodox account is rescued only by the Past Hypothesis, with Penrose's one-part-in-$10^{10^{123}}$ fine-tuning of the early-universe Weyl curvature as the honest measure of what this costs.


These three gaps are at the foundation of statistical mechanics. They have been discussed without resolution since the founding period of the subject (Loschmidt 1876, Zermelo 1896, Boltzmann 1877, Gibbs 1902, Einstein 1949). The structural barrier to closing them is uniform: *the orthodox program rests on time-symmetric microscopic dynamics, and a time-asymmetric output cannot follow rigorously from a time-symmetric foundation without an external auxiliary input*. The auxiliary inputs—the Stosszahlansatz, coarse-graining, the Past Hypothesis—have not themselves been derived from a deeper physical principle. The 150-year persistence of the gaps is not a failure of effort but a structural feature of any program built on time-symmetric mechanics alone.


### The Historical Asymmetry Among Foundational Programs


The structural significance of the present paper is best appreciated by comparing the foundational-derivation literature in the three sectors of physics—gravity, quantum mechanics, and thermodynamics—over the past century. The comparison reveals a pronounced asymmetry: gravity and quantum mechanics each have a *crowded foundational-principle literature*, with multiple programs proposing alternative derivations of the standard formalism from deeper physical sources; *thermodynamics has none*. The asymmetry is not subtle. It is the structural reason that Einstein's 1949 admission of thermodynamics as a "theory of principle" has stood unchallenged for three-quarters of a century.

The comparative table below catalogs the principal foundational-derivation programs in each sector. The criterion for inclusion is structural: the program must propose to *derive* the standard formalism of the sector—the Einstein field equations in gravity; the Schrödinger or Dirac equation, the canonical commutation relation, the Born rule in quantum mechanics; the Boltzmann–Gibbs postulates T1–T3, the Second Law, the arrow of time in thermodynamics—from a physical principle deeper than the formalism itself. Programs that interpret, reformulate, or extend the standard formalism without proposing such a derivation are excluded.


*[See PDF for tabular content.]*


The asymmetry is structural. The gravitational sector has been the subject of approximately fifteen to twenty distinct foundational-derivation programs over the past century, each proposing some alternative starting point for the Einstein field equations: the equivalence principle plus action principle (Einstein 1915), the Kaluza–Klein extra-dimension reduction (1921), Yang–Mills gauge structure, holographic emergence, string-theoretic compactification, twistor reformulation, and so on. The quantum-mechanical sector has been the subject of approximately twelve to fifteen such programs: the Dirac–von Neumann axioms, hidden-variables theories, Many-Worlds, decoherence-plus-Born-rule reductions, informational-reconstruction theorems, and so on. Each of these programs proposes a structural derivation of the formalism from a deeper physical or informational source, and each has been the subject of substantial subsequent literature.

The thermodynamic sector has been the subject of *zero* such programs. Boltzmann's 1872 H-theorem began as a foundational-derivation program—deriving entropy increase from the molecular-collision dynamics—but Boltzmann himself retreated from this in 1877 to a probabilistic reading after Loschmidt's reversibility objection (1876) made clear that the Stosszahlansatz could not be justified from time-symmetric microscopic dynamics alone. Jaynes 1957's Maximum-Entropy framework reformulates the probability measure in epistemic terms (subjective ignorance about microscopic state) but does not derive it from a physical principle deeper than the formalism. The Past Hypothesis (Albert 2000, Loewer 2007, Carroll 2010) proposes a cosmological boundary condition rather than a derivation. Jacobson 1995 derives the Einstein field equations as an equation of state, but this *imports* the Bekenstein–Hawking entropy formula and the Clausius relation as inputs—it is a derivation of *gravity from thermodynamics*, not a derivation of thermodynamics itself. Verlinde 2010's entropic gravity has the same structural import: thermodynamics is the *premise*, not the *conclusion*.

The result is the asymmetry shown in the table. A reader looking for the foundational-derivation literature in gravity finds dozens of papers spanning a century; the same reader looking for the foundational-derivation literature in quantum mechanics finds approximately the same number; the same reader looking for the foundational-derivation literature in thermodynamics finds *nothing*—a literature that does not exist.

The present paper closes this asymmetry. The McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$—already shown in [MGGRChain] to derive the Einstein field equations and the full content of general relativity, and in [MGQMChain] to derive the Schrödinger and Dirac equations and the full content of quantum mechanics—derives in addition the full content of thermodynamics: the probability measure, ergodicity, the Second Law, the arrows of time, the dissolutions of Loschmidt's objection and the Past Hypothesis, the Bekenstein–Hawking entropy, and the FRW cosmological-holography signature.

The historical first established by the present paper is therefore stronger than the corresponding firsts in the GR and QM sectors. The GR and QM chain papers join crowded literatures and stand out by their structural simplicity and unifying power; the present paper enters a literature that did not previously exist. And the principle that closes the 150-year gap is the same principle that closes the GR and QM gaps. **Three sectors of foundational physics—each with its own century-long history of unification attempts (in GR and QM) or 150-year stalemate (in thermodynamics)—now descend together, as theorems, from the same simple statement that the fourth dimension is expanding at the velocity of light.**


### The McGucken Principle as Foundational Source


The McGucken Principle [MGProof,MGGRChain,MGFQXi2008,MGSingular,MGPrinciple] states that the fourth dimension is expanding in a spherically symmetric manner at the velocity of light:

$$\frac{dx_4}{dt} = ic.$$

The principle asserts that $x_4$, the fourth coordinate of spacetime, is a real geometric axis advancing at the velocity of light from every spacetime event. The factor $i$ is the perpendicularity marker: $x_4$ is perpendicular to the three spatial dimensions $x_1, x_2, x_3$ in the same Pythagorean sense that the imaginary axis is perpendicular to the real axis on the complex plane. The Minkowski line element (induced by $x_4 = ict$, the integrated coordinate shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$) $ds^2 = dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2 + dx_4^2$ with $x_4 = ict$ reduces to $ds^2 = d\mathbf{x}^2 - c^2 dt^2$, and the McGucken Principle asserts that the manifold $\mathcal{M}$ of spacetime is foliated by spatial three-slices $\Sigma_t$ parameterized by $t$, with $x_4$ advancing perpendicular to each slice at rate $ic$.

**Critical clarification (load-bearing).** The form $x_4 = ict$ that historically appears in Minkowski's 1908 line element is the *integrated coordinate shadow* of the foundational dynamical principle $dx_4/dt = ic$. The principle is not a relabeling of $t$; it is the assertion that $x_4$ is an active, physical, geometric process that expands at velocity $c$ in a spherically symmetric manner from every spacetime event. The coordinate equation $x_4 = ict$ obtains as the time-integral of $dx_4/dt = ic$, viewed in a frame at rest with respect to the cosmological $x_4$-expansion. Every theorem in this paper traces to the *active expansion*; $x_4 = ict$ is its *mere integrated shadow*, not the foundational postulate.

The McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ states that the fourth dimension is expanding as a spherically-symmetric wavefront at the velocity of light from every spacetime event. The wavefront carries wavelength, frequency, phase, and action, so $c$ and $\hbar$ are twin properties of the one advance: the spinor is supported on a wavefront that already has the Compton frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$. The dynamical content of physics — the equations of Schrödinger, Dirac, Klein–Gordon, Maxwell, and Einstein — lives in the wavefront character of this expansion and is read from it directly.

This reading articulates a structural identity that the orthodox literature has not articulated: $c$ and $\hbar$ are not two independently postulated fundamental constants of nature. They are twin properties of the single wavefront expansion $dx_4/dt = ic$. The velocity $c$ is the radial expansion rate of the wavefront; Planck's constant $\hbar$ is the action quantum carried by the wavefront's phase content. The two constants emerge together because they are two readings of one object — they appear together because they describe two aspects of the same advance.

The specific consequences:

- *Wavelength on the wavefront.* The expanding wavefront carries a wavelength $\lambda = c/\nu$ at every point on its 2-surface, with the wavelength supplying the spatial scale of the wavefront's phase variation. The de Broglie relation $\lambda = h/p$ at the matter tier and the photon relation $\lambda = c/\nu = hc/E$ at the radiation tier are direct readings of the wavefront wavelength.

- *Frequency on the wavefront.* The wavefront carries a frequency $\nu$ at every point, with the Compton frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ supplying the matter-coupling rate (Theorem 4 of the present paper). The Planck–Einstein relation $E = h\nu$ at the radiation tier and the Compton-coupling identity $\omega_C \hbar = mc^2$ at the matter tier are direct readings of the wavefront frequency.

- *Phase on the wavefront.* The wavefront carries a phase $\phi = \omega_C t$ at every point, accumulated through the integrated $x_4$-advance. The Feynman path-integral phase $\exp(iS/\hbar)$ of quantum mechanics is the integrated wavefront phase along a worldline (Theorem 19 of the present paper, the Universal McGucken the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel Theorem); the canonical commutation relation $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$ of Theorem 19.1 / 19.2 / 19.3 is the operator-level reading of the same phase content.

- *Action on the wavefront.* The wavefront carries the action quantum $\hbar$ as the natural unit of phase: $\Delta\phi = \Delta S/\hbar$. The Schrödinger equation $i\hbar\,\partial\psi/\partial t = \hat H\psi$, the Heisenberg uncertainty relation $\sigma_q \sigma_p \ge \hbar/2$, the Bekenstein–Hawking entropy unit $\hbar G/c^3 = \ell_P^2$, and the Hawking temperature $T_H = \hbar a/(2\pi c\kB)$ all carry $\hbar$ because the wavefront whose expansion they describe carries the action quantum as its phase-content scale.

The Dirac equation $(i\gamma^\mu \partial_\mu - m)\psi = 0$ is the differential statement of how a spin-$1/2$ matter field rides the wavefront with the Compton frequency $\omega_C$ as its oscillation rate. The two-component Weyl spinor structure tracks the $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ rotational symmetry of the wavefront via the double cover $\mathrm{SU}(2) \to \mathrm{SO}(3)$.

- *Dynamics in the premise.* The wavefront character of $dx_4/dt = ic$ supplies all dynamical content of physics: the Schrödinger equation, the Dirac equation, the Klein–Gordon equation, the Maxwell equations, the Einstein field equations, and the wave equation are all differential statements of how matter and fields ride the same $x_4$-advance. ### Falsifiability of the Framework: Five Criteria


The McGucken framework is falsifiable both at the level of its individual theorems and at the level of the framework as a whole. Five distinct empirical and structural criteria specify how the framework would be refuted; we list them as D1–D5 and indicate which results in the present paper bear directly on each.

**D1 (The Compton-coupling diffusion at zero temperature).** The framework predicts a residual zero-temperature spatial diffusion coefficient $D_x^{(\mathrm{McG})} = \varepsilon^2 c^2 \Omega/(2\gamma^2)$ for any massive particle coupled to $x_4$'s expansion through the Compton-coupling ansatz of [2]MGCompton, where $\varepsilon$ is the dimensionless modulation amplitude (universal across species), $\Omega$ is the modulation angular frequency (universal across species; not the Compton frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ but an independent parameter of $x_4$'s expansion), and $\gamma$ is the environmental damping rate (residual gas collisions, trap-induced cooling, or engineered dissipation; species- and apparatus-dependent). The mass cancellation is exact: $D_p \propto m^2 c^2 \Omega$ and $D_x = D_p/(m\gamma)^2$, giving $D_x^{(\rm McG)}$ mass-independent at this order. The diffusion is present at $T\to 0$ and is temperature-independent. Theorem 14 (\S15) develops this prediction in full. The empirical content: cold-atom, trapped-ion, and precision-spectroscopy experiments are sensitive to $D_x$ at the level of $\varepsilon^2\Omega \lesssim 2 D_0^{\rm exp}\gamma^2/c^2$; if $\Omega$ is at the Planck frequency ($\sim 1.85\times 10^{43}$ Hz), current atomic-clock bounds on anomalous low-temperature diffusion constrain $\varepsilon \lesssim 10^{-20}$. The cross-species mass-independence is the sharp falsifiability content: residual diffusion ratios across species $A$ and $B$ with measured $\gamma$ should satisfy $D_{0,A}/D_{0,B} \approx (\gamma_B/\gamma_A)^2$, *independent* of $m_A/m_B$. A mass-dependent residual would falsify the Compton-coupling ansatz of Theorem 4 and the framework's Part III empirical signature.

**D2 (Compton-decoupling vanishing of matter entropy production, with the vacuum itself never decoupled).** A structural clarification is essential before stating the empirical content. *The vacuum is not external to $dx_4/dt = ic$ and cannot be decoupled from it.* Every point of spacetime is the apex of its own McGucken Sphere; the vacuum is itself *constituted* by $dx_4/dt = ic$ at every event. The active spherical expansion of $x_4$ at velocity $c$ from every spacetime event *is* what the vacuum is. There is no "decoupled-from-$x_4$ regime" for the vacuum to occupy. The Huygens-equals-Holography identification (Theorem 21) makes this explicit: every vacuum point carries an iterated McGucken Sphere structure whose surface holds $A/\ell_P^2$ independent $x_4$-modes per Planck cell, and the entire bulk structure of the vacuum is the continuous holographic content of these spheres. The vacuum is therefore the most $x_4$-coupled object in physics, not the least; it is the very medium of $x_4$'s expansion.

What *can* vanish is the Compton-coupling parameter $\varepsilon$ of *matter* to $x_4$'s phase oscillation. The Compton-coupling diffusion of Theorem 14, $D_x^{(\mathrm{McG})} = \varepsilon^2 c^2 \Omega/(2\gamma^2)$, vanishes quadratically in $\varepsilon$. In the structural limit $\varepsilon \to 0$ of zero Compton coupling *for a matter sector*, that matter sector's contribution to the strict Second Law of Theorem 9 vanishes: $dS_{\mathrm{matter}}/dt \to 0$. This is the empirical content of D2 properly stated: *matter* sectors with vanishing Compton coupling to $x_4$ contribute zero entropy production. #### Theorem (Carnot 1824 as Theorem of dx4/dt = ic)


*Statement.* The Carnot cycle bound — that no heat engine operating between reservoirs at temperatures $T_H$ and $T_C$ can have efficiency exceeding $\eta_{\rm Carnot} = 1 - T_C/T_H$ — is a theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ via the Geometric Channel reading of the $+ic$-monotonic content. The cycle is a *closed geometric path* on the indicator diagram of $(P, V)$ states, with the orientation of traversal encoded by the $+ic$-monotonic direction of $x_4$-expansion. The work extractable from one complete cycle is bounded by the $T_C/T_H$ factor because the heat-flow content carries the $+ic$ orientation of the McGucken Sphere expansion that drove it.

*Proof.* The Carnot cycle traverses four legs in $(P, V, T)$ phase space: isothermal expansion at $T_H$ (heat absorbed $Q_H$), adiabatic expansion ($T_H \to T_C$, no heat exchange), isothermal compression at $T_C$ (heat rejected $Q_C$), and adiabatic compression ($T_C \to T_H$, no heat exchange). The cycle is closed in $(P, V)$ space; its enclosed area equals the net work $W = Q_H - Q_C$ extracted per cycle.

*Step 1 (the cycle as a McGucken Sphere trajectory).* By Theorem 3 of the present paper (Huygens-wavefront propagation), every spacetime event is the apex of a forward McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(p_0)$ of radius $R(t) = c(t - t_0) > 0$ for $t > t_0$. The traversal of the Carnot cycle is a sequence of equilibrium states $\{s_1, s_2, s_3, s_4\}$ in $(P, V, T)$ phase space connected by quasi-static transitions; each transition is a path on the McGucken manifold $\mathcal{M}$ whose $x_4$-component advances monotonically at rate $ic$ by the Principle. The cycle is closed in $(P, V, T)$ but is *not* closed in $x_4$: the working substance advances by $\Delta x_4 = ic \cdot t_{\rm cycle}$ in the duration $t_{\rm cycle}$ required to complete the cycle, with the $+ic$ orientation of this advance being the load-bearing geometric content.

*Step 2 ($Q_H$ as $x_4$-coupled energy absorbed from the McGucken Sphere expansion of the hot reservoir).* By Theorem 4 (Compton coupling), every massive particle of the hot reservoir oscillates at the Compton frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ as it advances along $x_4$, with the rest-frame phase accumulation rate set by $dx_4/d\tau = ic$ on the four-velocity budget $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$. The hot reservoir at temperature $T_H$ has Boltzmann–Gibbs-distributed kinetic energies $\langle E \rangle \sim \kB T_H$ supplied by Compton-coupled $x_4$-phase fluctuations. The heat $Q_H$ absorbed from the hot reservoir during the isothermal expansion at $T_H$ is the integrated $x_4$-coupled energy transferred from the reservoir's Compton-modulated population to the working substance over the duration of the isothermal leg. By the spatial-projection isotropy of $x_4$-driven displacement (Theorem 5), this transfer respects the $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-symmetry of the McGucken Sphere structure.

*Step 3 ($Q_C$ as $x_4$-coupled energy rejected to the cold reservoir, with the $+ic$ orientation fixing the sign).* By Theorem 9b of the present paper, the net rate of kinetic-energy transfer between two Compton-coupled massive-particle ensembles in thermal contact at temperatures $T_H > T_C$ is strictly from hot to cold: $\dot Q_{H \to C} > 0$ strict, via the speed-asymmetry calculation of Compton-coupled Brownian interfacial flux closed by the strict Second Law of Theorem 9. The cold reservoir at temperature $T_C$ therefore absorbs $Q_C > 0$ from the working substance during the isothermal compression at $T_C$. Reversal of the transfer would invert the inequality (9b.14), violate Theorem 9, and contradict the $+ic$ orientation of $dx_4/dt = ic$. The Kelvin–Planck statement of the Second Law — no process whose sole result is the transfer of heat from a colder to a hotter body — is therefore a direct corollary of Theorem 9b.

*Step 4 (the Carnot efficiency bound as the $T_C/T_H$ factor of $+ic$-monotonic mode-counting).* By Theorem 9 of the present paper, the entropy of any massive-particle ensemble undergoing Compton-coupled Wiener-process diffusion is $S(t) = (3/2) \kB [1 + \ln(4\pi D t)]$ with $dS/dt = (3/2)\kB/t > 0$ strict. The reservoir entropy contributions per unit heat absorbed/rejected are $dS_H = Q_H/T_H$ (hot reservoir loses entropy at rate $Q_H/T_H$) and $dS_C = Q_C/T_C$ (cold reservoir gains entropy at rate $Q_C/T_C$). The total entropy change per cycle is $\Delta S_{\rm total} = -Q_H/T_H + Q_C/T_C$. By the $+ic$-monotonic content of the McGucken Second Law, $\Delta S_{\rm total} \geq 0$, with equality only for the reversible (Carnot) cycle. Solving for $W/Q_H = (Q_H - Q_C)/Q_H$ gives

$$\eta = \frac{W}{Q_H} = 1 - \frac{Q_C}{Q_H} \leq 1 - \frac{T_C}{T_H} = \eta_{\rm Carnot}.$$

The Carnot efficiency bound is the direct corollary of the $+ic$-monotonic content of $dx_4/dt = ic$ applied to the closed-cycle constraint that the working substance returns to its initial $(P, V, T)$ state after one cycle.

*Step 5 (the orientation of the cycle is the $+ic$ orientation of $x_4$).* The Carnot cycle traversed in the forward direction (heat engine: $Q_H$ absorbed hot, $W$ extracted, $Q_C$ rejected cold) corresponds to the $+ic$ orientation of $x_4$-expansion: the closed path on the indicator diagram is traced in the same orientation as the $+ic$-monotonic advance of $x_4$. The reverse traversal (refrigerator: $W$ input, $Q_C$ absorbed cold, $Q_H$ rejected hot) requires external work input precisely because reversing the cycle direction would correspond to reversing the $+ic$ orientation of $x_4$, which is forbidden by the Principle; the external work input is the compensation required to maintain the $+ic$-monotonic content of the overall process. The Carnot cycle bound is therefore forced by $dx_4/dt = ic$ via Theorems 3 (McGucken Sphere geometry), 4 (Compton coupling), 5 (spatial-projection isotropy), and 9 (strict Second Law), with the $+ic$-monotonic content supplying the closure that makes the cycle bound a theorem rather than a postulate. ∎

#### Theorem (Kelvin 1852 as Theorem of dx4/dt = ic)

*Step 3 (dissipation as entropy increase).* By Theorem 9 of the present paper (strict Second Law $dS/dt = (3/2)\kB/t > 0$ for massive-particle ensembles) and Theorem 10 (photon entropy $dS/dt = 2\kB/t > 0$ on the McGucken Sphere), the entropy of any $x_4$-coupled system increases monotonically with $t$. Kelvin's irreversibility is therefore the $+ic$-only content of the McGucken Sphere expansion.

Kelvin's 1852 statement is the conjunction of universality (Step 1), tendency/directionality (Step 2), dissipation as entropy increase (Step 3), and irreversibility (Step 4), each a direct consequence of $dx_4/dt = ic$. The statement is forced by the Principle. ∎

*Step 2 (entropy on the cosmological McGucken Sphere).* By Theorem 9 (strict Second Law for massive-particle ensembles) and Theorem 10 (photon entropy on the McGucken Sphere), every $x_4$-coupled system on the cosmological McGucken Sphere has entropy increasing at the rate $dS/dt = (3/2)\kB/t$ (massive matter) or $dS/dt = 2\kB/t$ (photons on the Sphere surface). $$\frac{dS_{\rm cosmological}}{dt} = \sum_{\rm subsystems} \frac{dS_i}{dt} + \frac{dS_{\rm photons}}{dt} + \frac{dS_{\rm horizons}}{dt} > 0,$$

with strict positivity supplied by the $+ic$ orientation of each summand (Theorems 9, 10, 15). The "tends toward a maximum" content of Clausius's statement is the strict positivity of $dS_{\rm cosmological}/dt$ combined with the asymptotic boundedness imposed by the Sphere's mode-count saturation.

Clausius's 1865 statement is forced by Theorems 9, 10, 15, 18, 21 of the present paper plus the cosmological McGucken Sphere of [MGCosHolo] §5 plus the $+ic$-monotonic content of the Principle. ∎

*Diagnostic remark.* Clausius's 1865 paper introduced the word "entropy" (from Greek $\tau\rho o\pi\eta$ for "transformation") and immediately deployed it at the cosmological scale, with the statement about the universe tending toward maximum entropy closing the paper. Clausius did not attempt a derivation from microscopic dynamics; he derived the statement from the impossibility of certain heat-flow patterns (the Clausius statement: no spontaneous heat flow from cold to hot). The derivation was pure the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel: a statement about which direction the propagation runs, with the $+ic$-monotonic content as load-bearing input. The cosmological scope was unproblematic to Clausius because the directionality is universal — every heat flow respects the $+ic$ orientation, so every entropy change in the universe respects the strict-positivity content. The McGucken framework supplies what Clausius did not have language to name: the structural source of the directionality is $dx_4/dt = ic$, with the $+ic$-monotonic content forcing the strict positivity of $dS/dt$ at every spacetime event of the cosmological McGucken Sphere.


#### The 1872 Channel-Switch: Boltzmann's Retrofit and Its Foundational Cost


The three the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel founders (Carnot 1824, Kelvin 1852, Clausius 1865) had established by 1865 the structural content of the Second Law as a directional/propagation fact: heat flows from hot to cold, mechanical energy dissipates, the entropy of the universe tends toward a maximum. The content is the Geometric Channel throughout: geometric, directional, $+ic$-monotonic in the McGucken language. No symmetry group, no atomic hypothesis, no statistical-mechanical machinery appears in any of the three founding statements.

Boltzmann's 1872 H-theorem [Boltzmann1872] attempted to *derive* this Geometric Channel content from the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel machinery: Hamiltonian time-symmetric atomic dynamics, the symplectic structure of phase space, the uniform Liouville measure as the equilibrium distribution. The attempt is structurally analogous to attempting to derive Huygens' Principle (the Geometric Channel, geometric propagation) from Stone's theorem on one-parameter unitary groups (the Algebraic Channel, algebraic symmetry): the two channels do not share machinery, and the derivation fails at the channel boundary unless an exogenous postulate supplies the missing $+ic$-monotonic content. Boltzmann supplied this postulate as the *Stosszahlansatz* — the assumption of molecular chaos before each collision — which is a time-asymmetric input smuggled into the time-symmetric Hamiltonian substrate.

Loschmidt's 1876 reversibility objection [Loschmidt1876] is the structural recognition that the smuggling is irrecoverable: for any solution $x(t)$ of time-symmetric Hamiltonian dynamics, the time-reversed trajectory $x(-t)$ is also a solution, so any entropy-increasing trajectory has an entropy-decreasing counterpart of equal Liouville-measure weight in the ensemble. Boltzmann's 1877 statistical reformulation [Boltzmann1877] relocates the directionality from the dynamics to an *initial-condition* postulate (the universe started in a low-entropy state), which is the same the Geometric Channel content reintroduced at a different structural layer. Zermelo's 1896 recurrence objection [Zermelo1896] is the parallel structural recognition that Poincaré recurrence (an Algebraic Channel theorem of Hamiltonian flow) directly contradicts strict monotonicity of any phase-space functional in the long-time limit.

The two objections are unanswerable from inside the Algebraic Channel. The Algebraic Channel is time-symmetric by construction; the Geometric Channel's $+ic$-monotonic content cannot be derived from time-symmetric machinery without an exogenous postulate. The Boltzmann–Gibbs program from 1872 to 1902 was therefore an Algebraic Channel retrofit of the original the Geometric Channel founders' content, and the retrofit was incomplete at every structural step where the Geometric Channel's directionality content was required.

The cost of the retrofit was Einstein's three gaps T1–T3 of Einstein's Three Gaps: T1 (the probability measure on phase space is postulated rather than derived) is the cost of attempting to extract the Geometric Channel's $+ic$-monotonic content from the Algebraic Channel's symmetry-respecting equilibrium structure; T2 (the equality of time-average and ensemble-average is not derivable from Hamiltonian dynamics alone) is the cost of attempting to extract the Geometric Channel's Huygens-wavefront identity (Theorem 8 of the present paper) from the Algebraic Channel's time-symmetric symmetry group; T3 (the Second Law's strict monotonicity is unanswerable from time-symmetric dynamics) is the direct cost of the channel-switch. All three gaps are artifacts of the 1872 retrofit, not features of the underlying physics.


#### Why the Algebraic Channel Machinery Was Chosen: The 1872–1902 Historical Pressures


The Boltzmann–Gibbs retrofit was not an arbitrary methodological choice. Specific historical, institutional, and structural pressures pushed the late-19th-century thermodynamic community toward the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel machinery despite the founding triad's clear the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel content. We catalogue the principal pressures so that the channel-switch is understood as historically forced rather than perversely chosen.

*Pressure 1: The mechanical-philosophy programme.* The late-19th-century physics community was committed to the *mechanical philosophy* — the doctrine that all physical phenomena reduce to the motion of particles under deterministic forces obeying Newton's laws of motion. Helmholtz 1847 [Helmholtz1847] had unified mechanics, heat, light, and electromagnetism under the single principle of energy conservation, and the success of this unification motivated the extension to thermodynamics: if heat is molecular motion (Mayer 1842 [Mayer1842], Joule 1843 [Joule1843]), then thermodynamics must reduce to mechanics. The mechanical-philosophy programme is structurally an Algebraic Channel programme: it commits to Hamiltonian time-symmetric dynamics as the foundational layer, which is the algebraic-symmetry content of physics. The founders' The Geometric Channel directional content was incompatible with this commitment because the Geometric Channel is irreducibly time-asymmetric (the McGucken Sphere expands forward, never backward), whereas Hamiltonian dynamics is time-symmetric by construction. The mechanical philosophy therefore *required* the channel-switch as the price of incorporating thermodynamics into the unified mechanical worldview.

*Pressure 2: The success of kinetic theory.* Maxwell's 1860 [Maxwell1860] derivation of the velocity distribution from uniformity in phase-space directions, and Maxwell–Boltzmann's subsequent 1860–1871 development of kinetic theory, supplied immense empirical success for the Algebraic Channel machinery: heat capacity ratios, transport coefficients, the equation of state of dilute gases, and the equipartition theorem all emerged from symmetry-respecting equilibrium analysis without need of the Geometric Channel directional content. The empirical success was so striking that the Algebraic Channel programme appeared self-evidently correct, and the absence of directional content in the equilibrium results was easy to overlook. The directional content of Carnot, Kelvin, and Clausius applied only to non-equilibrium processes (cycles, dissipation, entropy increase); the equilibrium phenomena that kinetic theory explained were precisely the cases where the Algebraic Channel's time-symmetric machinery sufficed. The structural distinction between equilibrium (the Algebraic Channel natural) and non-equilibrium (the Geometric Channel natural) was not recognized as a channel distinction; it was misread as a methodological convenience.

*Pressure 3: The atomic hypothesis.* The atomic hypothesis — that matter is composed of discrete atoms in motion — was contested in the late 19th century (Ostwald, Mach, and the energeticist school opposed atomism into the 1900s). Boltzmann's H-theorem was, among other things, a *defense* of the atomic hypothesis: by deriving the Second Law from atomic collisions, Boltzmann sought to demonstrate that atomism was sufficient to explain macroscopic thermodynamics. The defense required the Algebraic Channel machinery (Hamiltonian dynamics of atomic collisions, symplectic phase space, the Liouville measure on $6N$-dimensional space) because that was the only formalism available for "atoms in motion." The Geometric Channel directional content of Carnot–Kelvin–Clausius was, on this reading, *what needed to be explained*, not what should be taken as foundational. The atomic-hypothesis defense therefore committed the programme to deriving the Geometric Channel content from the Algebraic Channel machinery — which is structurally impossible without an exogenous postulate, as Loschmidt 1876 demonstrated within four years.

*Pressure 4: The differential-equation paradigm.* The 19th-century mathematical-physics tradition had decisively committed to differential-equation formulations of fundamental physics: Newton's equations, Lagrange's equations, Hamilton's equations, Maxwell's equations, Laplace's equation. All of these are *time-symmetric*: replacing $t \to -t$ leaves the equation form invariant. The paradigm itself privileged the Algebraic Channel machinery because differential equations encode local algebraic-symmetry content (the symmetry group of the equation under reparametrisation) rather than global geometric-propagation content (the directional propagation of solutions). Carnot's cycle, Kelvin's universal tendency, and Clausius's cosmological entropy maximum were *not* phrased as differential equations and were therefore institutionally suspect from the differential-equation perspective. Boltzmann's H-theorem reformulated the Second Law as $dH/dt \leq 0$, a differential-equation-style local statement, which made the content institutionally legible at the cost of channel-switching from B to A.

*Pressure 5: The Lagrangian–Hamiltonian formalism as the prestige formalism.* By 1872 the Lagrangian and Hamiltonian formulations of mechanics (Lagrange 1788, Hamilton 1834) had become the prestige formalisms of theoretical physics: any new physical theory was expected to admit a Lagrangian or Hamiltonian formulation as the test of its fundamental status. The Geometric Channel directional content of the founders was incompatible with this formalism (the Hamiltonian is conserved under time-translation, so a Hamiltonian-derived Second Law must be Hamiltonian-consistent and therefore time-symmetric). Boltzmann's H-theorem fit the prestige formalism by deriving the Second Law from atomic Hamiltonians; the cost was the channel-switch and the resulting need for the Stosszahlansatz as exogenous input.

*Pressure 6: The institutional separation of thermodynamics and statistical mechanics.* By 1900 thermodynamics (the macroscopic phenomenology of Carnot, Kelvin, Clausius) and statistical mechanics (the microscopic mechanism of Boltzmann, Gibbs) were treated as two separate disciplines, with thermodynamics relegated to engineering and statistical mechanics elevated to fundamental physics. The institutional hierarchy reinforced the channel-switch: the Geometric Channel was the methodology of the engineering discipline (thermodynamic cycles for heat-engine design), the Algebraic Channel was the methodology of the fundamental discipline (statistical mechanics for foundational understanding). The hierarchy obscured the structural fact that Geometric Channel's directional content was the *foundational* content while the Algebraic Channel's symmetry content was the *complementary* content; instead, the Algebraic Channel was treated as foundational and the Geometric Channel as derivative.

The six pressures collectively *forced* the channel-switch as the historically rational choice given the institutional and methodological commitments of 1872. The cost was the foundational gaps — but the cost was not visible until Loschmidt 1876 made the structural impossibility explicit, and even then the gaps were absorbed into the Algebraic Channel programme as features (the Stosszahlansatz as auxiliary assumption, the Past Hypothesis as boundary condition, the Maximum Entropy reformulation as epistemic principle) rather than recognized as channel-switch artifacts. The McGucken framework is structurally novel precisely because it operates *outside* all six pressures: it is not committed to mechanical reduction (it derives mechanics from $dx_4/dt = ic$, not the reverse); it does not privilege equilibrium over non-equilibrium (it derives both as channels of the same Principle); it does not require the atomic hypothesis as foundational (atoms are derived structures, not primitives); it admits non-differential-equation foundational statements ($dx_4/dt = ic$ is an *equation*, but its content is geometric propagation, not local algebraic dynamics); it does not require the Lagrangian–Hamiltonian formalism as the prestige formalism (the Lagrangian appears as the $x_4$-phase accumulation of [Proposition L.3]MGUnification, derived rather than postulated); it does not separate thermodynamics from statistical mechanics (Theorems 9 and 7 are parallel the Geometric Channel and the Algebraic Channel theorems of the same Principle).


#### The Structural Inevitability of Asymmetry Loss Under the Algebraic Channel Formalization


The deeper structural fact behind the 1872 channel-switch is that *$dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel machinery is constitutively time-symmetric*. The algebraic-symmetry content of any physics treats T-reversal as a discrete symmetry of the Poincaré group; any derivation built on symmetry-respecting machinery (Hamiltonian flow, symplectic phase space, Liouville measure, unitary representations, Stone's theorem, Noether currents) is time-symmetric by construction. When the late-19th-century community chose the Algebraic Channel machinery to *formalize* what Carnot/Kelvin/Clausius had stated as directional propagation facts, the very act of choosing the Algebraic Channel *guaranteed* the loss of the $+ic$-orientation. The asymmetry could not survive the formalization because the formalism itself does not admit asymmetry as primitive content.

The loss is structural, not contingent. To see this, we name the principal the Algebraic Channel objects and verify their time-symmetry:

1. *Hamilton's equations* $\dot{q} = \partial H/\partial p$, $\dot{p} = -\partial H/\partial q$ are invariant under $t \to -t$, $p \to -p$ (and $q \to q$). Any trajectory $\gamma(t)$ admits a time-reversed trajectory $\gamma(-t)$ as an equally valid solution. The +ic-orientation cannot be encoded in Hamiltonian dynamics.

2. *Liouville's theorem* preserves the symplectic measure under Hamiltonian flow in both forward and reverse time directions. The measure cannot distinguish past from future.

3. *The canonical commutation relation* $[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$ is invariant under $t \to -t$ together with complex conjugation (anti-unitary T-reversal of Wigner 1932). The +ic content of $\hbar$ is not the same as the $+ic$ orientation of $x_4$-expansion; it is a symmetry-respecting content that admits a T-reversed counterpart.

4. *Stone's theorem* on one-parameter unitary groups guarantees the existence of self-adjoint generators for *both* forward and reverse translations along any parameter, including time. The generator $\hat{H}$ of time translation admits the anti-unitary T-reversal as a symmetry; the $+ic$ direction is not selected.

5. *Noether's theorem* derives conserved currents from symmetries; symmetries are by definition time-symmetric (a symmetry that distinguished past from future would not be a symmetry). All Noether currents are therefore time-symmetric.

6. *The Lagrangian* $L = T - V$ and the action $S = \int L \, dt$ are invariant under $t \to -t$ (with appropriate sign flips of momenta). The principle of stationary action $\delta S = 0$ admits time-reversed extremals as equally valid.

7. *The Hilbert space inner product* $\langle \psi_1 | \psi_2 \rangle$ admits anti-unitary T-reversal $\hat{T}|\psi\rangle = |\psi^*\rangle$ such that $\langle \hat{T}\psi_1 | \hat{T}\psi_2 \rangle = \langle \psi_2 | \psi_1 \rangle$, preserving probabilities under T. The +ic-orientation is not encoded in the inner-product structure.

8. *Unitary evolution* $|\psi(t)\rangle = e^{-i\hat{H}t/\hbar}|\psi(0)\rangle$ is reversible: $|\psi(0)\rangle = e^{+i\hat{H}t/\hbar}|\psi(t)\rangle$. The forward and backward evolutions are equally valid; the $+ic$ direction is not selected by the formalism.

All eight the Algebraic Channel objects are structurally time-symmetric. None of them can serve as the carrier of $+ic$-monotonic content. Any derivation of the Second Law that uses only these objects must either *fail* (Loschmidt 1876, Zermelo 1896) or *smuggle in* a time-asymmetric postulate from outside the formalism. The smuggling is the channel-switch artifact.

The McGucken framework's $+ic$-orientation is, by contrast, encoded in the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel objects that *are* directionally asymmetric by construction:

1. *The forward McGucken Sphere* $\Sigma_+(p_0)$ has radius $R(t) = c(t - t_0) > 0$ for $t > t_0$ and is undefined (or has formally negative radius) for $t < t_0$. The Sphere expands forward, never backward; its very definition includes the $+ic$-orientation.

2. *Huygens-wavefront propagation* (Theorem 3 of the present paper) sends every point on a wavefront forward as the source of new wavelets; there is no backward-propagation primitive.

3. *Compton-coupled Brownian motion* (Theorem 6 of the present paper) has strictly positive diffusion coefficient $D > 0$, with the sign coming directly from the $+ic$ orientation of $x_4$-expansion. A reversal would require $dx_4/dt = -ic$, contradicting the Principle.

4. *The cosmological McGucken Sphere* of [MGCosHolo] §5 has radius $R_4(t) = c(t - t_0) > 0$ with the origin event $t_0$ as the apex of the Sphere; the lowest-entropy moment is geometrically forced as the origin, not statistically fine-tuned.

The Geometric Channel objects are *constitutively asymmetric*; the Algebraic Channel objects are *constitutively symmetric*. The 1872 channel-switch lost the asymmetry not by accident but by the structural commitments of the formalism chosen. The McGucken framework recovers the asymmetry by recognizing that the founders' The Geometric Channel objects are theorems of $dx_4/dt = ic$ rather than mere phenomenological surrogates, with the asymmetry encoded in the geometry itself.


#### The Four Post Hoc Remedies and Their Structural Cost


Given the asymmetry loss under the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel formalization, the late-19th and 20th-century thermodynamic community pursued four distinct post hoc remedies to reintroduce the missing $+ic$-orientation. Each remedy is a different way of smuggling the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel content back into the Algebraic Channel formalism after the formalization has stripped it. We catalogue the four remedies and their structural costs.

*Remedy 1: Ignore the asymmetry.* Gibbs's 1902 [Gibbs1902] *Elementary Principles in Statistical Mechanics* explicitly restricts attention to equilibrium thermodynamics, where time-symmetric machinery suffices. The arrow of time is set aside as a separate problem; the formalism handles only the symmetric content (partition functions, equilibrium ensembles, equilibrium fluctuations). This is the *epistemic-honesty* remedy: it acknowledges that Algebraic Channel cannot supply the Geometric Channel content and chooses to address only the Algebraic Channel content. The cost is that the Second Law's directional content — the original Carnot–Kelvin–Clausius content — is excluded from the foundational formalism. Non-equilibrium thermodynamics becomes an applied science rather than foundational physics.

*Remedy 2: Insert a time-asymmetric assumption (the Stosszahlansatz).* Boltzmann's 1872 [Boltzmann1872] H-theorem inserts the *Stosszahlansatz* — the assumption that the velocities of two molecules about to collide are statistically uncorrelated — as an exogenous time-asymmetric input. The assumption is time-asymmetric because correlations *after* a collision are non-zero (the molecules have just interacted); applying the Stosszahlansatz to the *before*-state and not the *after*-state is a directional commitment imported from outside the Hamiltonian dynamics. The cost is the foundational status of the Second Law: it is no longer a theorem of mechanics but a theorem of mechanics-plus-the-Stosszahlansatz, with the latter being a postulate at the same logical level as the Second Law itself. Loschmidt 1876 made this cost explicit: the Stosszahlansatz cannot be derived from Hamiltonian dynamics because it is time-asymmetric and Hamiltonian dynamics is time-symmetric.

*Remedy 3: Insert a time-asymmetric initial condition (the Past Hypothesis).* Boltzmann's 1877 [Boltzmann1877] statistical reformulation, developed in modern form by Albert 2000 [Albert2000], Loewer 2007, Carroll 2010 [Carroll2010], and Penrose's 1989 Weyl Curvature Hypothesis [Penrose1989], relocates the time-asymmetric content from the dynamics to the *initial condition* of the universe. The dynamics remain time-symmetric (Hamiltonian, Liouville-preserving); the universe is *postulated* to have started in an extraordinarily low-entropy state (Penrose's $10^{-10^{123}}$ Weyl-curvature fine-tuning is the quantitative measure). The cost is the immense fine-tuning of the initial condition, which is then defended as a brute fact about the universe rather than explained. The Geometric Channel directionality is preserved but at the cost of a cosmological postulate of staggering improbability. This is the *cosmological-postulate* remedy.

*Remedy 4: Relocate the asymmetry into epistemology (Maximum Entropy).* Jaynes 1957 [Jaynes1957] reformulates statistical mechanics as a procedure for *inferring* probability distributions from incomplete information, with the maximum-entropy distribution being the unique inference-respecting choice. The directional content of the Second Law is reinterpreted as an epistemic content: an observer with limited information about a system will assign probabilities that maximize entropy subject to known constraints; as the observer's information becomes outdated relative to the system's evolution, the entropy of the observer's probability distribution increases. The cost is that the Second Law becomes a fact about observers rather than a fact about the universe. The Geometric Channel objective directionality of Carnot–Kelvin–Clausius is replaced with a subjective epistemic principle, dissolving the foundational status of the Law as a feature of physical reality. This is the *epistemic-reduction* remedy.

The four remedies are not exclusive — Boltzmann combined Remedies 2 (Stosszahlansatz) and 3 (low-entropy initial condition); Jaynes combined Remedies 1 (equilibrium focus) and 4 (epistemic reduction); Carroll combined Remedies 3 (Past Hypothesis) and an extension to multiverse statistical reasoning. But all four share the common structural feature that the $+ic$-orientation is inserted *post hoc*, after the Algebraic Channel formalization has stripped it, with the insertion location varying (assumption layer, initial-condition layer, epistemic layer, or formal-exclusion layer) but the insertion content being the same: directional information that the formalism could not generate on its own.

The McGucken framework eliminates all four remedies because it does not need them. The $+ic$-orientation is built into the Geometric Channel objects (the McGucken Sphere expands forward by construction); the directionality is encoded in the geometry, not in an auxiliary postulate. The Stosszahlansatz is replaced by Theorem 12 (the Loschmidt dissolution: time-symmetric the Algebraic Channel dynamics and time-asymmetric the Geometric Channel propagation coexist at structurally different levels of the same Principle). The Past Hypothesis is replaced by Theorem 13 (the lowest-entropy moment is geometrically forced as the origin of the cosmological McGucken Sphere). The Jaynes epistemic reduction is replaced by the McGucken Duality (the Second Law is objectively true as a Geometric Channel theorem; the epistemic content is a separate matter about observer access to microstates). The exclusion of non-equilibrium content is replaced by Theorems 9, 10, 14, 15 (the full non-equilibrium chain as theorems of $dx_4/dt = ic$).

The structural diagnostic: every post hoc remedy of the 20th-century thermodynamic tradition is a Geometric Channel insertion forced by the Algebraic Channel formalization's inability to generate directional content. The McGucken framework eliminates the need for the insertions by restoring the Geometric Channel at the foundational level, with both channels descending from $dx_4/dt = ic$ as parallel theorems.

### Survey of Seventeen Prior Foundational Programs in Thermodynamics


The McGucken framework's structural novelty is best characterized by comparison with the prior foundational programs that have addressed Einstein's three gaps T1–T3 in the orthodox Boltzmann–Gibbs program. We catalog seventeen such programs, indicating for each what it derives, what it postulates, and the structural difference from the McGucken approach. The first fifteen span the period 1872–2010 (statistical-mechanical and thermodynamic-spacetime programs); the sixteenth is Marletto's 2016 constructor theory of thermodynamics, treated in greater depth in the constructor-theory analysis below as a recent addition to the Cascade of Near-Misses; the seventeenth is Barbour's shape-dynamics / Janus-point cosmology (1999–2020), treated in greater depth in the Barbour analysis below as a sustained five-decade challenge to the entropy-time-arrow program.


1. **Boltzmann's H-theorem (1872).** Boltzmann derived the entropy-increase H-theorem from the Stosszahlansatz applied to molecular collisions. *Postulates*: the Stosszahlansatz (assumption of molecular chaos before each collision); the existence of a uniform Liouville measure on phase space; the time-symmetric Hamiltonian dynamics. *Derives*: the H-theorem $dH/dt \leq 0$ under the Stosszahlansatz. *Structural difference*: the Stosszahlansatz is a time-asymmetric assumption smuggled into a time-symmetric substrate; the McGucken framework derives the Second Law from $x_4$'s monotonic expansion at $+ic$ without smuggling.
2. **Maxwell's velocity distribution (1860).** Maxwell derived the velocity distribution of an ideal gas from uniformity in phase-space directions. *Postulates*: uniform measure on velocity directions. *Derives*: the Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution. *Structural difference*: Maxwell's uniformity is the algebraic-symmetry content of $x_4$'s spherical isotropy; the McGucken framework derives the same uniformity as a theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ (Theorem 5).

Both descend from the same single principle $dx_4/dt = ic$.
4. **Gibbs ensemble framework (1902).** Gibbs introduced canonical, microcanonical, and grand canonical ensembles. *Postulates*: principle of equal a priori probabilities; uniform Liouville measure; existence of a thermal-equilibrium ensemble. *Derives*: equilibrium thermodynamics from the partition function. *Structural difference*: the Gibbs ensemble framework is the algebraic structure of equilibrium thermodynamics; the McGucken framework derives the underlying probability measure (Theorem 7) as theorem rather than postulate.
5. **Einstein 1905 Brownian motion.** Einstein derived $D = \kB T/(6\pi\eta r)$ connecting molecular collisions to macroscopic diffusion. *Postulates*: molecular-kinetic hypothesis; equipartition theorem. *Structural difference*: Einstein's derivation is the macroscopic-microscopic bridge in the orthodox program; the McGucken framework derives the same diffusion as a theorem of $x_4$-driven displacement (Theorem 6), with the empirical signature $D_x^{(\mathrm{McG})} = \varepsilon^2 c^2 \Omega/(2\gamma^2)$ of Theorem 14 being the framework-specific extension to zero-temperature regimes.

Constructor theory is in addition treated formally in the cascade-of-near-misses analysis of the constructor-theory analysis, where it is identified as the most recent (2013–2025) empirical surfacing of the Geometric Channel without the active-expansion content of $dx_4/dt = ic$.

The McGucken framework treats time as the integrated coordinate shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$ (i.e., $x_4 = ict$ is a real coordinate on the McGucken manifold $\mathcal{M}$), the Janus point as the McGucken origin event $t_0$ where the cosmological McGucken Sphere has radius zero, and the Second Law as the forced theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ (Theorem 9 of the present paper). The bidirectionality of Barbour's Janus point is rejected by the $+ic$-monotonic content of the McGucken Sphere (only future-directed expansion at velocity $c$, no $-ic$ branch). Barbour's empirical observation that cosmic structure grows is reconciled with the Second Law via the local-vs-global distinction: local subsystem structure grows while global cosmological McGucken Sphere entropy strictly grows monotonically, as the McGucken Sphere expansion supplies the universal entropy reservoir to which local subsystems export entropy. ### Position in the Three-Paper Series on dx4/dt = ic


The present paper is the third in a three-paper series that derives the foundational content of physics as theorems of the McGucken Principle. The first paper [MGGRChain] derives general relativity as a chain of theorems descending from $dx_4/dt = ic$, including the Einstein field equations, the Schwarzschild metric, the gravitational time-dilation factor, and a Part IV extending into black-hole thermodynamics, the Susskind holographic program, the GKP–Witten AdS/CFT dictionary, Penrose's twistor theory, the Arkani-Hamed–Trnka amplituhedron, and Witten's 1995 string-theory dynamics with M-theory unification, all as theorems of $dx_4/dt = ic$. The second paper [MGQMChain] derives quantum mechanics as a chain of twenty-one theorems including the Schrödinger and Dirac equations, the canonical commutation relation $[\hat{q},\hat{p}] = i\hbar$ (doubly derived through Hamiltonian and Lagrangian routes), the Born rule, the Feynman path integral, and the full Feynman-diagram apparatus of quantum field theory. The present paper completes the series by deriving thermodynamics as a chain of eighteen theorems.


### Organization of the Paper


The paper is organized in four parts. **Part I (Foundations: \S2–7)** establishes the foundational theorems descending from $dx_4/dt = ic$ that supply the kinematic substrate for thermodynamics: the wave equation from Huygens' Principle, the spatial isometry group $\mathrm{ISO}(3)$ as the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel symmetry group, the Huygens-wavefront propagation as the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel geometric content, the Compton coupling, the spatial-projection isotropy, and Brownian motion. **Part II (Three Resolutions of Einstein's Gaps: \S8–10)** closes Einstein's three gaps: the probability measure as Haar measure, ergodicity as Huygens-wavefront identity, and the Second Law as strict $dS/dt > 0$. **Part III (Arrows of Time, Architectural Resolutions, Empirical Signature: \S11–15)** develops the photon entropy, the five arrows of time, the structural dissolution of Loschmidt's objection, the dissolution of the Past Hypothesis, and the Compton-coupling diffusion as empirical signature. **Part IV (Black-Hole Thermodynamics and Cosmological Holography: \S16–19)** extends the chain into the semiclassical-gravity regime via the McGucken Wick rotation. Each theorem has formal statement, formal proof, plain-language explanation, and explicit comparison with the standard derivation.

\S20 synthesizes the chain. \S21 develops the dual-channel content of the master equations $dS/dt = (3/2)\kB/t$ and $dS_{BH}/dA = \kB/(4\lP^2)$. \S22 concludes Parts I–IV. \S23 catalogs the source-paper provenance with the corpus extension. \S24 records the Princeton-origin Era I–V chronology. \S25 lists all references in the Bibliography.

**Step B3 (Direct verification of the wave equation).** Compute the partial derivatives of $\psi$ from (the spherical ansatz). The time derivative:

$$\frac{\partial^2 \psi}{\partial t^2} = \frac{c^2 f''(r - ct) + c^2 g''(r + ct)}{r}.$$

$$\nabla^2 \psi = \frac{1}{r^2}\frac{\partial}{\partial r}\left(r^2 \frac{\partial \psi}{\partial r}\right) = \frac{1}{r}\frac{\partial^2 h}{\partial r^2}.$$

With $h(r,t) = f(r-ct) + g(r+ct)$, the second radial derivative is $h_{rr} = f''(r-ct) + g''(r+ct)$, giving

$$\nabla^2 \psi = \frac{f''(r-ct) + g''(r+ct)}{r}.$$

Therefore

$$\frac{1}{c^2}\frac{\partial^2 \psi}{\partial t^2} - \nabla^2 \psi = \frac{f''(r-ct) + g''(r+ct)}{r} - \frac{f''(r-ct) + g''(r+ct)}{r} = 0$$

## Theorem 2: The Algebraic-Symmetry Content of dx4/dt = ic as the Spatial Isometry Group ISO(3)


**Theorem (Algebraic-Symmetry Content).** The algebraic-symmetry content of the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ is the spatial isometry group

$$\mathrm{ISO}(3) = \mathrm{SO}(3) \ltimes \mathbb{R}^3,$$

the semidirect product of spatial rotations $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ and spatial translations $\mathbb{R}^3$. This is the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel content from which the probability measure on phase space (Theorem 7) descends.


### Proof (Theorem 2)


*Proof.* The proof is direct inspection of the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$: the algebraic-symmetry group ISO(3) appears as an immediate consequence of three structural features of the Principle, with no external mathematical input. Start with the McGucken Principle in its physical-geometric content: $x_4$ advances at the constant rate $ic$ from every spacetime event, with the expansion proceeding in a spherically symmetric manner. We catalog the symmetries (in the sense of group actions that fix the Principle's statement) and identify the resulting group.


**(i) Temporal uniformity.** The rate $dx_4/dt$ equals the constant $ic$, independent of $t$. Under temporal translation $t \mapsto t + \Delta t$, the principle's content is invariant. This generates a one-parameter subgroup $\mathbb{R}_t$ of time-translations.


**(ii) Spatial homogeneity.** The principle holds at every spacetime event, with no preferred spatial origin: for any $\Delta\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{R}^3$, translation $\mathbf{x}\mapsto \mathbf{x} + \Delta\mathbf{x}$ leaves the principle's content unchanged. This generates the abelian subgroup $\mathbb{R}^3$ of spatial translations.


**(iii) Spherical isotropy.** The expansion of $x_4$ is spherically symmetric: it has no preferred spatial direction. For any $\mathcal{O}\in\mathrm{SO}(3)$, the rotation $\mathbf{x}\mapsto \mathcal{O}\mathbf{x}$ leaves the principle's content unchanged. This generates the subgroup $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ of rotations.


**(iv) Combining (ii) and (iii) on each spatial slice $\Sigma_t$.** The relevant group on the spatial three-slice is the smallest group containing both $\mathbb{R}^3$ and $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ such that the action is consistent: rotations act on translation vectors, $\mathcal{O}\cdot \Delta\mathbf{x} = \mathcal{O}\Delta\mathbf{x}$. By definition of semidirect product, this is

$$\mathrm{ISO}(3) := \mathrm{SO}(3) \ltimes \mathbb{R}^3$$

with group multiplication $(\mathcal{O}_1, \mathbf{a}_1)(\mathcal{O}_2, \mathbf{a}_2) = (\mathcal{O}_1\mathcal{O}_2, \mathbf{a}_1 + \mathcal{O}_1 \mathbf{a}_2)$.


**(v) Topological structure.** The group $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ is a compact Lie group (homeomorphic to $\mathbb{RP}^3$, by the standard double-cover $\mathrm{SU}(2) \to \mathrm{SO}(3)$ identifying antipodes on $S^3$; see Bröcker–tom Dieck 1985, *Representations of Compact Lie Groups* §I.1 [BrockerTomDieck1985]); $\mathbb{R}^3$ is a locally compact abelian Lie group. The semidirect product $\mathrm{ISO}(3)$ inherits local compactness; it is a Lie group of dimension $3 + 3 = 6$. This local compactness will be load-bearing for Theorem 7.


**(vi) Uniqueness as algebraic-symmetry content.** The group $\mathrm{ISO}(3)$ is the *unique* algebraic-symmetry content of $dx_4/dt = ic$ at the spatial-three-slice level, in the sense that:

- any subgroup omits one of (i)–(iii), which are all forced by the principle;
- any supergroup includes a transformation that does not preserve the principle's content (e.g., dilations $\mathbf{x}\mapsto\lambda\mathbf{x}$ would alter the spherical-radius rate).

The Lorentz-covariance of the rate $dx_4/dt = ic$ extends $\mathrm{ISO}(3)$ to its Poincaré cover $\mathrm{ISO}(1,3)$ in four dimensions [MGNoether]. For thermodynamic applications restricted to spatial slices $\Sigma_t$, the relevant group is $\mathrm{ISO}(3)$; for applications involving Lorentz boosts (e.g., relativistic statistical mechanics), the group is the full Poincaré group. The present paper restricts attention to $\mathrm{ISO}(3)$ for the probability-measure derivation in Theorem 7. ∎

There is no separate the Geometric Channel derivation of ISO(3) as such, because ISO(3) is not derived from the geometric-propagation content but *is* the algebraic-symmetry content. ## Theorem 3: The Geometric-Propagation Content of dx4/dt = ic as Huygens-Wavefront Propagation on the McGucken Sphere


**Theorem (Geometric-Propagation Content).** The geometric-propagation content of the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ is the Huygens-wavefront propagation on the McGucken Sphere of radius $R(t) = ct$ expanding from every spacetime event. This is the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel content from which ergodicity (Theorem 8) and the Second Law (Theorem 9) descend.


### Proof (Theorem 3)


*Proof.* From Theorem 1, the wave equation (the wave equation) describes spherically-symmetric expansion at speed $c$ from any spacetime event, and (the wave equation) is itself the differential statement of $dx_4/dt = ic$. We now exhibit the geometric content of this propagation.


**Step 1 (Definition of the McGucken Sphere).**

**Definition.** For any spacetime event $p_0 = (\mathbf{x}_0, t_0)\in\mathcal{M}$, the *McGucken Sphere* $\Sigma_+(p_0)$ is the locus of spacetime events reachable from $p_0$ by null geodesics of the Minkowski metric (the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$):

$$\Sigma_+(p_0) := \{(\mathbf{x},t)\in\mathcal{M} : |\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}_0| = c(t-t_0),\ t > t_0\}.$$

This is the future light cone of $p_0$. In any spatial three-slice $\Sigma_t$ with $t > t_0$, the McGucken Sphere intersects $\Sigma_t$ in a two-sphere of radius $R(t) = c(t - t_0)$ centered on $\mathbf{x}_0$.


**Step 2 (Huygens' Principle as iterated McGucken Sphere).** Huygens' Principle (1690) [Huygens1690] states that every point on a wavefront acts as a source of secondary wavelets, and the new wavefront at time $t + \Delta t$ is the envelope of these secondary wavelets centered on the wavefront at time $t$, each with radius $c\Delta t$. We formalize this as a theorem: in the McGucken framework, Huygens' Principle is the iterative geometric content of the McGucken Sphere. The strong Huygens property — that wave propagation from a point source has support strictly on the future null cone, not in its interior — is itself a theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ via the dimension count of the spatial slice $\Sigma_t \cong \mathbb{R}^3$: the spatial three-slice on which $x_4$'s spherical-symmetric expansion at velocity $c$ projects is odd-dimensional (specifically $n = 3$), and the strong Huygens property holds in odd spatial dimensions $\geq 3$ but fails in even spatial dimensions (Hadamard 1923 [Hadamard1923]; Friedlander 1975 [Friedlander1975]).


**Lemma (Iterative McGucken Sphere).** Let $W(t) := \Sigma_+(p_0)\cap\Sigma_t$ be the McGucken Sphere from $p_0$ in the spatial slice $\Sigma_t$. For each point $q\in W(t)$, let $\Sigma_+(q)$ denote the McGucken Sphere of $q$, and let $W_q(t+\Delta t) := \Sigma_+(q)\cap \Sigma_{t+\Delta t}$. Then

$$W(t+\Delta t) \;=\; \partial\!\left(\bigcup_{q\in W(t)} W_q(t+\Delta t)\right)_{\rm outer},$$

where $\partial(\cdot)_{\rm outer}$ denotes the outer boundary (the envelope of the union).

*Proof of lemma.*
By Definition~def:McGSphere, $W(t+\Delta t) = \{(\mathbf{x},t+\Delta t) : |\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}_0| = c(t+\Delta t - t_0)\}$. For any such point $\mathbf{x}$, let $\hat{\mathbf{n}} = (\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}_0)/|\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}_0|$, and define $q := (\mathbf{x}_0 + c(t-t_0)\hat{\mathbf{n}}, t)\in W(t)$. Then $|\mathbf{x} - (\mathbf{x}_0 + c(t-t_0)\hat{\mathbf{n}})| = c\Delta t$, so $(\mathbf{x},t+\Delta t)\in W_q(t+\Delta t)$, proving $W(t+\Delta t) \subseteq \bigcup_q W_q(t+\Delta t)$. Conversely, any point $(\mathbf{x},t+\Delta t) \in \bigcup_q W_q(t+\Delta t)$ has $|\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}_0| \leq c(t-t_0) + c\Delta t$ by the triangle inequality, with equality (i.e., the outer boundary of the union) precisely when the radial direction from $q$ matches the radial direction from $p_0$. The outer boundary therefore recovers exactly $W(t+\Delta t)$. $\Box$ ∎


**Step 3 (Geometric monotonicity).** The radius $R(t) = c(t-t_0)$ is monotonically increasing in $t$, with derivative $dR/dt = c > 0$. The McGucken Sphere therefore grows monotonically in volume $V(t) = (4/3)\pi R^3(t)$ and surface area $A(t) = 4\pi R^2(t)$, with no possibility of contraction. This monotonicity descends directly from the foundational physical-geometric fact that $dx_4/dt = ic$ — the fourth dimension's expansion at velocity $c$ is monotonic and one-way at $+ic$ — and is the structural source of the Second Law (Theorem 9).


**Step 4 (One-way advance at $+ic$).** The McGucken Principle in its physical-geometric form states that the fourth dimension is *actively expanding* at velocity $c$ in a spherically symmetric manner; the rate $dx_4/dt = ic$ has the orientation $+ic$, not $-ic$. The integrated coordinate shadow $x_4 = ict$ inherits this one-way orientation: $x_4$ advances forward, never backward. The McGucken Sphere therefore expands forward in $t$, not backward. This time-orientation is the structural source of the arrow of time (Theorem 11). There is no counterpart expansion at $-ic$ in physical reality; the advanced Green's function of (the wave equation), which would propagate backward in $t$, is not physically realized. The $+ic$-monotonicity is *load-bearing*: every irreversibility theorem of the present paper (Theorems 9, 10, 11, 12, 13) traces back to this orientation choice fixed by the active expansion at $+ic$.


The $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel content of $dx_4/dt = ic$ is therefore: the McGucken Sphere expanding at rate $c$ from every event, with monotonic volume and surface-area growth and one-way time-orientation. This geometric-propagation content is the source of the irreversibility theorems of Part II. $\Box$ ∎


### Comparison with Standard Derivation


Huygens' 1690 derivation of wave propagation by spherical secondary wavelets was a phenomenological account of light propagation: every wavefront point acts as a source. The principle was successful but had no deeper geometric source until the McGucken framework. In the McGucken framework, Huygens' Principle is the geometric content of $dx_4/dt = ic$ at the spatial-three-slice level, with the wavefront being the cross-section of the McGucken Sphere expanding from each event. The iterative structure of Huygens' Principle is iterative McGucken Sphere expansion, and the monotonic radial growth of the Sphere is the structural source of the irreversibility theorems of Part II.

**In plain language.** Huygens' Principle says: every point on a wavefront sends out new little spherical wavelets. In the McGucken framework, this is just the geometric content of the principle $dx_4/dt = ic$: from every spacetime event, $x_4$ expands like a sphere at speed $c$, and every point of that sphere is itself the source of a new sphere. Crucially, the sphere only grows—it never contracts. This monotonic growth of the McGucken Sphere is what eventually gives us the Second Law of Thermodynamics.
