*(H4) The entropic-force adiabatic clarification — Verlinde's own response to questioner pressure.* The Verlinde 2011 paper has often been read by orthodox physicists as claiming that gravity is a "$dS/dx$-force" — a force generated by the *change* in entropy as a test particle moves toward a holographic screen. Verlinde 2022 explicitly corrects this misreading, *in response to direct questioning at the end of the talk*:

> *Questioner (paraphrased): I'm confused — your polymer example shows a force from a change in entropy $dS/dt$, but your gravity story talks about $S$ itself, not $dS/dt$.*

The actual equation here is that when you lower the speed [of the polymer end] you're doing it adiabatically — because if that would not have been [done by a] force, the entropy would have changed. So the force is actually making sure that the entropy does not change, but the consequence of the force is the tendency to change the entropy. So this is a reversible system."*  
>   — Verlinde 2022, [VerlindeIAS2022], minutes 41:13–41:50

The structural content: entropic forces in Verlinde's sense are *reversible / adiabatic* — they are conservative forces derived from an entropy potential, in the same way that electromagnetic forces are derived from the electromagnetic potential. *(H5) Verlinde's own self-acknowledgment of programmatic incompleteness.* The Verlinde 2022 talk closes with explicit honest admissions:

> *"I think if we really want to discuss this very seriously I should develop the theory of emerging gravity much further. We should have some way of deriving dynamics and having some analog of the Friedmann equation or something that at least we can derive from this microscopic picture. What I've done here is a very simple thing: I basically took my phenomenological relation and put it in the Friedmann equation and see somebody what is the consequence."*

These admissions are the primary-source acknowledgment from the corpus author himself that (a) the entropic-gravity programme lacks a derivation of cosmological dynamics analogous to the Friedmann equation from the microscopic substrate, and (b) the Hubble-tension applications Verlinde sketches are explicitly speculative pending such development.

### Theorem 19.4.4.5: The Common Six-Step Methodology of Gravity-from-Entropy Programs — Structural Convergence Diagnosis, the Field's Second Blind Spot, and What the Uniformity of Terminology Reveals

**Preamble.** Theorems 19.4.3 and 19.4.4 have identified Jacobson 1995 and Verlinde 2011 individually as proper structural subsets of the McGucken framework. The present theorem generalizes the diagnosis. It states that *every* gravity-from-entropy program in the orthodox literature — Jacobson 1994 (entanglement entropy + Sakharov induction), Jacobson 1995 (local Rindler horizons + Clausius), Padmanabhan 2005–2012 (horizon degrees of freedom + equipartition), Verlinde 2010 (holographic screens + entropic force), Van Raamsdonk 2010 / Ryu–Takayanagi 2006 (entanglement entropy on AdS boundary), Parikh–Svesko 2018 (stretched light cones at every event), Alonso-Serrano–Liberati 2020 (causal-diamond thermodynamics), Bianconi 2024 (quantum relative entropy between two metrics) — executes the same six-step methodology in the same order, with the "differences" among the programs consisting only of the specific noun chosen for each slot. The structural convergence, when read against the linguistic uniformity of the field's popular presentations ("Entropy = Gravity," "Gravity from Entropy," "Entropic Gravity," "Thermodynamics of Spacetime"), is the sociological signature of a deeper physical fact that the field has systematically declined to articulate: the programs are not competing derivations of gravity from thermodynamics; they are competing readings of a single underlying object which none of them has named.

Under the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ that object is named. ### Corollary 19.4.4.5.1: Ontological Reading of the Convergence — What the Uniformity Tells Us About Physical Reality

The convergence of the orthodox gravity-from-entropy programs on the same conclusion (gravitational content extracted from thermodynamic content, via one of six variations on the same six-step skeleton) is not a coincidence, and it is not an artifact of overlapping technical vocabulary. It is the empirical signature of a foundational physical fact: *gravity and thermodynamics are dual-channel readings of one underlying physical-geometric principle*. The four programs each catch part of this principle and read off part of its consequences; none names the principle. The McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ names it.

Specifically: the convergence tells us that (i) there exists a single object at every spacetime event — the McGucken Sphere, the spherically-symmetric wavefront of $x_4$'s expansion at $c$ — that is simultaneously the arena all four programs postulate; (ii) this object carries an entropy that all four programs identify with area; (iii) this object carries a temperature that all four programs identify with the Hawking/Unruh form; (iv) this object supports the equilibrium condition all four programs postulate as "extremely good approximation"; (v) this object's dynamics produces the Einstein field equations that all four programs recover. The programs did not stumble on gravity from entropy by four different accidents; they read the same wavefront by four different names. Once the name is supplied — $dx_4/dt = ic$ — the convergence dissolves from mystery into forced consequence: any observer who identifies part of the wavefront's structure will derive part of gravity from part of thermodynamics, in the specific limit accessible to their vocabulary. Jacobson 1995 reads the null-surface face and gets Einstein equations from Clausius. Verlinde 2010 reads the screen face and gets Newton's laws from entropic force. Jacobson 1994 reads the entanglement-across-horizon face and gets $S_{\rm BH}$ from induced gravity. Bianconi 2024 reads the matter-induced-metric face and gets modified Einstein from quantum relative entropy. All four are correct within their scope; all four are proper structural subsets of the same underlying wavefront reading.

The convergence question the field has not asked is precisely the question the McGucken framework answers with a Corollary rather than with a theorem, because the answer requires no additional theorem: it requires only the observation that when six independent research programs starting from independent premises converge on the same conclusion via six variations on the same methodology, the shared substrate is *not* a coincidence to be catalogued but a physical fact to be named. The field has not named it because the field has not asked the question. The present corollary asks the question and names the answer: the substrate is $dx_4/dt = ic$, and the wavefront is the McGucken Sphere.


### Corollary 19.4.4.5.2: Diagnosis of the Field's Silence — Why the Convergence Question Has Been Systematically Avoided

The sociological factors that have kept the convergence question off the agenda of the orthodox literature are diagnosable as follows. First, *academic differentiation incentives*: research programs are rewarded for staking distinct territory ("my derivation transcends Jacobson's because it derives inertia," "my theory is not horizon-based, unlike Verlinde and Jacobson," "my program uses entanglement entropy, not thermodynamic entropy"). The convergence question — "why do we all get gravity from entropy?" — is structurally in tension with differentiation because it invites the answer "because we are all reading the same underlying object," which reduces the programs' claimed originality to a shared substrate they have not named. The differentiation incentive is stronger than the unification incentive at the publication level, and stronger still at the popular-media level, where video titles emphasize "Erik Verlinde: Why My Entropic Gravity Transcends Jacobson's" rather than "Why Jacobson and I Are Both Reading the Same Physical Object Without Naming It."

Second, *terminological homonym-mistaken-for-difference*: Bianconi's presentation of her "quantum relative entropy" as "not the horizon entropy of Verlinde or Jacobson" [BianconiJaimungal2024] is a homonym issue treated as a foundational one. Horizon entropy is entropy attached to a two-surface with the area-law form; quantum relative entropy on the Araki algebra of two metric-density operators reduces, in the horizon limit, to the same area-law form. The two entropies are not "unrelated"; they are the same object read on different mathematical substrates. Presenting them as unrelated is a linguistic convenience that hides the structural convergence. The same applies to the polymer-entropic-force reading of Verlinde 2010, the entanglement-entropy reading of Jacobson 1994, the Clausius-heat reading of Jacobson 1995, and the quantum-relative-entropy reading of Bianconi 2024. All four are readings of area-law entropy on a null-ish surface, differentiated by mathematical vocabulary rather than by underlying content.

Third, *the two-decade proliferation of clickbait titles*: The popular-media presentation of gravity-from-entropy programs has, over the last decade and a half, converged on a small vocabulary — "Entropy = Gravity," "Gravity from Entropy," "Entropic Gravity," "The Physicist Who Derived Gravity from Entropy," "Gravity Linked to Thermodynamics," "Intriguing Study Explains Gravity Through Quantum Entropy" — which is linguistically identical across programs that the presenters simultaneously insist are foundationally different. Sample video-title inventory (each program's popular presentation, chronological): "The Physicist Who Proved Entropy = Gravity" (Jacobson, Curt Jaimungal channel); "Erik Verlinde: Why My Entropic Gravity Transcends Jacobson's" (Verlinde, Jaimungal); "The Physicist Who (Unexpectedly) Derived Gravity From Entropy" (Bianconi, Jaimungal); "Entropic Gravity from Quantum Entanglement! | with Erik Verlinde" (Verlinde interview); "Emergence of Gravity from Quantum Information" (Verlinde talk title); "Gravity Linked to Thermodynamics in Black Holes" (Jaimungal channel summary); "Intriguing Study Explains Gravity Through Quantum Entropy" (Bianconi popular coverage). The vocabulary uniformity is the sociological signature of the structural convergence: presenters converge on the same terminology because they are, in fact, describing the same object.

The diagnostic conclusion is that the convergence question has been avoided not because it is difficult but because it is *awkward*: asking it makes the differentiation claims of individual programs harder to sustain. ### Remark 19.4.4.5.1: The Verlinde-vs-Jacobson Dispute as Intra-Methodology, Not Inter-Methodology

Verlinde's stated distinction from Jacobson — "Jacobson basically assumed spacetime already, and just derived Einstein equations from it; I derive inertia as well, so my program is more fundamental" [VerlindeJaimungal2024 minute 1:24–3:41] — is not a foundational difference but an intra-methodology one. Both programs execute the same six-step skeleton of Table \ref{tab:six-step-skeleton}. Verlinde substitutes a holographic screen at $\Phi = \Phi_0$ for Jacobson's local Rindler horizon (a swap within slot S1), substitutes a bit count with equipartition for Jacobson's $S = \eta A$ (a swap within slot S2), and substitutes the Compton-wavelength entropy jump for Jacobson's Raychaudhuri-focusing (a swap within slot S4). These are three lateral swaps within the same methodology; they do not constitute a distinct methodology. Verlinde's claim to "transcend" Jacobson is the claim that his substitutions in slots S1, S2, S4 yield $F = ma$ as an additional output — which is a legitimate observation about the coverage of his substitutions but is not a claim to have derived gravity from a foundation Jacobson lacked. Both programs derive gravity from the same six-step methodology; Verlinde's derivation covers one additional cell of the output (inertia) that Jacobson's covers only implicitly. Neither program supplies the physical substrate that would ground the methodology.

Similarly, Bianconi's stated distinction — "my quantum relative entropy is not the horizon entropy of Verlinde or Jacobson" [BianconiJaimungal2024] — is a substitution within slot S2 (entropy attached to arena), not a departure from the six-step skeleton. Bianconi's arena (slot S1) is a matter-induced metric rather than a horizon; her entropy (slot S2) is quantum relative entropy on Araki algebras rather than area entropy; her thermodynamic identity (slot S4) is variational extremization rather than Clausius. These are three lateral substitutions, not a distinct methodology. The output (slot S5) recovers modified Einstein equations at low coupling — the same output all four programs deliver.

- *Entanglement entropy* (J94): $S_{\rm ent} = -\mathrm{tr}\,\rho_I\ln\rho_I$ where $\rho_I$ is the reduced density matrix on one side of a bipartition. In the horizon limit with Planck-scale cutoff, $S_{\rm ent} \to A/(4\hbar G_{\rm ren})$.

All four converge on the Bekenstein–Hawking entropy $S_{\rm BH} = k_B A/(4\ell_P^2)$ in the horizon limit. The convergence is not accidental; it is forced by the fact that all four are readings of *Planck-cell mode counting on a two-surface*, which is the McGucken framework's derivation of $S_{\rm BH}$ (Theorem 15). The mathematical substrates differ; the underlying object is identical. Bianconi's "geometric quantum relative entropy" is not the opposite of "horizon entropy" and it is not a special case of horizon entropy in any structurally interesting sense — it is the same Planck-cell mode-counting object read on a different mathematical apparatus, delivering the same area-law behavior in the appropriate limit.

The linguistic contrast "quantum relative entropy \emph{versus} horizon entropy" is a homonym confusion. The entropies are all the same physical object. The formalisms differ; the physics does not.

The three additions together answer the convergence question the field has not asked: *why can gravity be derived from entropy by so many parties using so many methods?* Because gravity, entropy, thermodynamics, nonlocality, and the metric are siblings, and any research program that identifies part of the shared source will derive part of the family resemblance. The programs converge because they are reading the same object — not because gravity emerges from thermodynamics, and not because thermodynamics emerges from gravity, but because both emerge from $dx_4/dt = ic$ as parallel theorems that do not pass through one another.


### Remark 19.4.4.6.2: The Sociological Consequence — A Better Popular Presentation

The consequence of Corollary 19.4.4.6.3 is that the popular presentations of the gravity-from-entropy programs — the video-title inventory of Remark 19.4.4.5.3 — should be reframed. Rather than "Erik Verlinde: Why My Entropic Gravity Transcends Jacobson's" (which presupposes a lineage), or "The Physicist Who (Unexpectedly) Derived Gravity From Entropy" (which suggests unlikely convergence), or "The Physicist Who Proved Entropy = Gravity" (which conflates identity with derivation), the honest popular framing under Theorem 19.4.4.6 would be: *Why the Four Independent Programs That Derive Gravity from Entropy Are All Reading the Same Wavefront Without Naming It, and What the Wavefront Is.* The convergence is the newsworthy fact; the naming of the wavefront ($dx_4/dt = ic$) is the answer to the convergence question; and the observation that gravity, entropy, thermodynamics, and nonlocality are four children of one parent — rather than a lineage in which each derives from the previous — is the diagnostic that dissolves the field's thirty-year quarrel over ordering. Videos framed as *"How Jacobson, Verlinde, Bianconi, and McGucken All Reach Gravity Through Entropy — And Why the Convergence Is the Deeper Physics"* would treat the field's convergence pattern as the primary discovery it structurally is, rather than as a background against which each program's individual "transcendence" is showcased.

### Theorem 19.4.4.7: Jacobson 1995 as the Founder of the Gravity-from-Entropy Programme — Historical Priority, Structural Depth, and Every Subsequent Program Measured as Distance from His Original Insight

**Preamble.** The present theorem redresses a historical omission that could otherwise be read into the parallel-column presentations of Theorems 19.4.4.5 and 19.4.4.6, which for diagnostic purposes tabulated Jacobson 1994, Jacobson 1995, Verlinde 2010, and Bianconi 2024 as four archetypes of one methodology. That tabulation is analytically correct but historically flat: Jacobson 1995 is *not* a peer of Verlinde 2010 or Bianconi 2024. Jacobson is the *founder* — the pioneer of the entire gravity-from-entropy programme, whose eight-page 1995 letter *Thermodynamics of Spacetime: The Einstein Equation of State* [Jacobson1995] opened the field and to which every subsequent program in the thirty-year lineage is downstream, explicitly and by direct citation. Verlinde 2010 [Verlinde2011] states in his own Section 5.2 that he adapts *"a similar reasoning as Jacobson"* to time-like screens. Padmanabhan 2002–2012 [Padmanabhan2005, Padmanabhan2010] extends Jacobson to FRW apparent horizons and to any diffeomorphism-invariant gravity theory. Bianconi 2024 [Bianconi2024] cites Jacobson 1995 directly (her reference [7]) as the ancestor of the entropic-action approach. Van Raamsdonk 2010, Ryu–Takayanagi 2006, Maldacena–Susskind 2013, Parikh–Svesko 2018, Alonso-Serrano–Liberati 2020, and Bianconi 2024 are all children of Jacobson in the specific sense that each cites him and takes some ingredient of his construction (the entropy-area proportionality, the Clausius relation, the local equilibrium assumption, the horizon-thermodynamic architecture) as given, then substitutes another ingredient.

The present theorem gives Jacobson his due: it details his seminal move, catalogues the three foundational depths he supplied that all subsequent work relies on, measures every subsequent program as *distance from Jacobson* rather than as peer of Jacobson, and — most importantly — reads Jacobson's own 1995 confession about "non-equilibrium spacetime" as the direction from which $dx_4/dt = ic$ arrives. The McGucken Principle is what Jacobson himself hoped someone would eventually find. Recognizing this is the correct honor to pay him, and it also correctly locates the McGucken framework in the field's intellectual lineage: not as competitor to Jacobson, but as the physical mechanism Jacobson explicitly said would be needed to close his own construction.


**Theorem 19.4.4.7 statement (five parts).**

*(I) (Historical priority.)* The gravity-from-entropy programme begins in 1995 with Jacobson's *Thermodynamics of Spacetime: The Einstein Equation of State* [Jacobson1995]. Prior work — Bekenstein 1973 [Bekenstein1973], Bardeen–Carter–Hawking 1973 [BCH1973], Hawking 1975 [Hawking1975], Unruh 1976 [Unruh1976], Gibbons–Hawking 1977 [GibbonsHawking1977], Bombelli–Koul–Lee–Sorkin 1986 [Bombelli1986], 't Hooft 1993 [tHooft1993], and Susskind 1994 [Susskind1994] — established the thermodynamic properties of horizons but did *not* derive gravitational dynamics from thermodynamic content. That inverse move — reading the Einstein field equations as an equation of state, with thermodynamic content as input and gravitational content as output — is Jacobson's, in 1995, and it is his alone. The eight-page letter is the pivot around which the entire subsequent thirty-year literature rotates. Every gravity-from-entropy paper after 1995 that derives Einstein equations from a thermodynamic identity is walking, in some direction, on Jacobson's ground.

*(II) (The seminal move.)* Jacobson's argument is structurally three moves executed in fifteen equations:

- *Move 1 (universal horizon architecture)*: Every spacetime point $p$ carries local Rindler causal horizons through it in every null direction. Consequently, the horizon-thermodynamic apparatus of Bekenstein–Hawking–Unruh applies *at every event*, not merely at black-hole event horizons — a universalization of horizon thermodynamics to a local diagnostic.
- *Move 2 (heat as boost energy across the horizon)*: The heat flux $\delta Q$ across the local Rindler horizon is defined as the integrated boost-energy current $\int_H T_{ab}\chi^a d\Sigma^b$, where $\chi^a$ is the approximate boost Killing field vanishing at the reference two-surface $P$ and $T_{ab}$ is the matter stress-energy tensor. Temperature is the Unruh temperature $T = \hbar\kappa/(2\pi)$ seen by the accelerated observer just inside the horizon. Entropy variation is $dS = \eta\,\delta A$ with $\eta$ a proportionality constant.
- *Move 3 (Clausius closes to Einstein via Raychaudhuri)*: Imposing $\delta Q = TdS$ on every local Rindler horizon at every spacetime point, and closing the identity with the Raychaudhuri equation $d\theta/d\lambda = -\tfrac{1}{2}\theta^2 - \sigma^2 - R_{ab}k^ak^b$ applied to the null generators, forces $T_{ab}k^ak^b = (\hbar\eta/2\pi)R_{ab}k^ak^b$ for all null $k^a$. Local energy conservation and the contracted Bianchi identity then close the algebra to $R_{ab} - \tfrac{1}{2}Rg_{ab} + \Lambda g_{ab} = (2\pi/\hbar\eta)T_{ab}$: the Einstein field equations, with $G = (4\hbar\eta)^{-1}$ identifying Newton's constant.

The move is that gravitational dynamics is not fundamental *because* it is the equation of state of the horizon-thermodynamic content of spacetime. Jacobson's own summary: *"it may be no more appropriate to canonically quantize the Einstein equation than it would be to quantize the wave equation for sound in air."* This is not a modest claim. It is the assertion that gravity is emergent thermodynamics — the sound of quantum spacetime, not one of its atoms — and it is the seminal statement of the entire subsequent literature.

*(III) (The three foundational depths.)* Jacobson supplied three structural depths that every subsequent gravity-from-entropy program still relies on, either explicitly (by citation) or implicitly (by architectural inheritance):

- *Depth 1 (universalization of the horizon)*: Before Jacobson, horizon thermodynamics was a diagnostic for specific horizons — black-hole event horizons, cosmological horizons, Rindler horizons of specific accelerated observers. After Jacobson, the horizon is a *local diagnostic at every event*. This universalization is the load-bearing structural move for Van Raamsdonk (entanglement across every bipartition), Verlinde (holographic screens at every equipotential), Padmanabhan (apparent horizons at every FRW slice), Parikh–Svesko (stretched light cones at every event), and Jacobson 2015 (causal diamonds at every event). Each subsequent program specializes or generalizes Jacobson's universalization.
- *Depth 2 (heat-as-boost-energy)*: Jacobson's identification of heat with the integrated boost-energy current across the horizon is the load-bearing thermodynamic bridge that makes $\delta Q = TdS$ well-defined at every event. Verlinde's entropic force $F\Delta x = T\Delta S$, Padmanabhan's equipartition on horizon DOFs, Bianconi's variational entropy extremum, and every entanglement-based programme in the lineage all rely on some form of Jacobson's bridge — a locally-defined thermodynamic quantity that couples to gravitational content.
- *Depth 3 (Raychaudhuri as the closing identity)*: The null-congruence equation is what makes Jacobson's derivation work: it converts the area-variation condition into a curvature condition. Every subsequent program that recovers Einstein equations by a similar route uses either Raychaudhuri directly (Padmanabhan, Verlinde in Section 5.2 via Komar mass and Killing vectors — "using a similar reasoning as Jacobson"), or a mathematical cousin (Wald's Noether-charge formalism, Iyer–Wald entropy, the Ryu–Takayanagi minimal-surface prescription).

Every subsequent program in the field inherits at least one of these three depths from Jacobson. Most inherit all three.

*(IV) (Every subsequent program as measured distance from Jacobson.)* Under Depths 1–3 as the reference axes, each subsequent program can be located by the specific ingredients it substitutes for Jacobson's originals. Table \ref{tab:jacobson-distance} makes this precise: each row is a Jacobson ingredient; each column is a subsequent program; each cell records the specific lateral swap the program makes from Jacobson's original construction. What emerges from the table is that no subsequent program departs from Jacobson at the *foundational* level (the three depths of Part III); every subsequent program departs from Jacobson only at the *lateral* level (which specific arena, which specific entropy expression, which specific thermodynamic identity fills each slot). The programs are not competitors of Jacobson at the foundational level; they are lateral variations on his construction. Jacobson is the founder, and every subsequent program is a child.

*(V) (Jacobson's 1995 confession points at $dx_4/dt = ic$.)* Jacobson's own closing paragraph in the 1995 letter is remarkable for what it acknowledges. He writes that his derivation *"presumed the existence of local equilibrium conditions"* and that at a *"deeper level, we also assumed the usual form of short distance vacuum fluctuations in quantum fields ... this also amounts to a sort of local equilibrium assumption. This deeper assumption is probably valid only in some extremely good approximation."* And then — the sentence that a physicist in 1995 might have thought was closing a modest speculation but that a physicist in 2026 can read as prophecy: *"We speculate that out of equilibrium vacuum fluctuations would entail an ill-defined spacetime metric. ... It is my hope that, by following this line of inquiry, we shall eventually reach an understanding of the nature of 'non-equilibrium spacetime'."*

That is precisely $dx_4/dt = ic$. The McGucken Principle *is* non-equilibrium spacetime: the fourth dimension is not in equilibrium; it is actively expanding at rate $c$ from every event. Local equilibrium in Jacobson's sense is not an approximation to be corrected but the wrong frame entirely — spacetime is not near-equilibrium, it is spherically expanding. Jacobson in 1995 hoped that a deeper physical understanding of non-equilibrium spacetime would emerge; that understanding is what the McGucken Principle supplies. Corollary 19.4.4.7.2 makes this precise.

### Corollary 19.4.4.7.1: The Lineage — Every Subsequent Program is a Lateral Variation on Jacobson's Six Ingredients

Under the diagnostic of Table \ref{tab:jacobson-distance}, the thirty-year post-1995 gravity-from-entropy literature can be organized as a lineage in which Jacobson is the pioneer and every subsequent program is a lateral variation. Specifically:

- *Padmanabhan 2005–2012* varies Jacobson's arena (from local Rindler horizons to FRW apparent horizons) and generalizes his gravity output (from Einstein equations to any diffeomorphism-invariant gravity theory). Same three foundational depths.
- *Verlinde 2010* varies Jacobson's arena (from null Rindler wedges to time-like holographic screens at equipotential surfaces) and adds a Compton-wavelength entropy postulate to derive $F = ma$ in addition to Einstein equations. Same three foundational depths — Verlinde himself writes in Sec.\ 5.2 that he uses *"a similar reasoning as Jacobson."*
- *Verlinde 2016* varies the 2010 construction to a de Sitter cosmological arena with an "elastic" dark-matter-like response, using the same holographic-screen apparatus. Same three foundational depths.
- *Van Raamsdonk 2010 / Ryu–Takayanagi 2006 / Maldacena–Susskind 2013* vary Jacobson's entropy expression (from horizon area entropy to entanglement entropy across bipartitions) and vary his arena (from local Rindler horizons to entanglement-cutting surfaces in AdS/CFT). Same three foundational depths — the universalization is now to every bipartition rather than every event, and the entropy is the entanglement entropy across the cut.
- *Parikh–Svesko 2018* varies Jacobson's arena (from local Rindler wedges to stretched light cones at every event) with a stretched-length parameter added. Same three foundational depths — a direct Jacobson-style application on a new type of null surface.
- *Jacobson 2015 (causal diamonds, entanglement equilibrium)* is Jacobson himself varying his 1995 construction (from local Rindler horizons to causal diamonds at every event), with entanglement entropy as the entropy expression. Same three foundational depths — Jacobson extending his own founding move.
- *Alonso-Serrano–Liberati 2020* extends Jacobson 2015 causal-diamond thermodynamics to nonequilibrium extensions and higher-curvature gravity. Same three foundational depths.
- *Bianconi 2024* varies Jacobson's arena (from horizons to matter-induced metrics on the Lorentzian manifold) and varies his entropy expression (from horizon area entropy to quantum relative entropy on Araki algebras of rank-2 tensor operators). Same three foundational depths — the universalization is now to every point of the manifold, and the entropy is a KL-type divergence, but the closing move is variational extremization inheriting Wald's Noether-charge apparatus and reducing to Jacobson's Einstein equations at low coupling.

The organizing principle: *every post-1995 program is Jacobson-with-a-lateral-swap.* The differences from Jacobson are real and each program contributes something genuinely additive; the shared inheritance from Jacobson is deeper than any of the differences. This is the honest structural read of the field's lineage.


### Corollary 19.4.4.7.2: What Only $dx_4/dt = ic$ Supplies Beyond Jacobson — the Answer to Jacobson's Own Closing Question

Jacobson 1995 confessed five undelivered inputs to his own construction, in his own paper's closing paragraph and in the details of his construction:

- *(J-U1)* Local equilibrium as approximation ("probably valid only in some extremely good approximation").
- *(J-U2)* The entropy coefficient $\eta$ undetermined, hence Newton's constant $G = (4\hbar\eta)^{-1}$ fitted rather than derived.
- *(J-U3)* The cosmological constant $\Lambda$ appearing as an integration constant with no fixed value ("as enigmatic as ever").
- *(J-U4)* Time-symmetric output (the Einstein equations) from time-asymmetric input (the Clausius $\delta Q = TdS$ with $dS \geq 0$) — the direction of time not derived.
- *(J-U5)* The direction toward which resolution should be sought: *"an understanding of the nature of 'non-equilibrium spacetime'."*

Under the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, each of Jacobson's five confessions is closed:

Verlinde's stated distinction from Jacobson — most explicitly in the 2024 Jaimungal interview [VerlindeJaimungal2024], but present in the 2010 paper's Sec.\ 6.1 as well ("*we have added an important element that is new. By adapting his reasoning to this situation, and combining it with Wald's exposition of the Komar mass, it is straightforward to construct an argument that naturally leads to the Einstein equations."* Verlinde's relativistic content is his own admission a Jacobson-style construction adapted to time-like screens. Both rest on the same three foundational depths (universalization of horizon, heat as thermodynamic bridge, Raychaudhuri/Wald closure). Both inherit the same confessed undelivered inputs. Neither derives the arrow of time.

Verlinde's genuine contribution is real (the $F = ma$ derivation is his own), and he deserves credit for it. What is misleading is the "transcends Jacobson" framing at the foundational level; at that level, Verlinde does not transcend Jacobson — he executes a lateral variation on Jacobson's construction. The correct framing under Table \ref{tab:jacobson-distance} is that Verlinde 2010 is Jacobson 1995 with a substituted arena (time-like screens instead of null Rindler wedges) and one additional derived relationship ($F = ma$), inheriting the same three foundational depths and the same undelivered inputs.

## Theorem 19.5: Channel Asymmetry — the Algebraic Channel is Lorentzian-Locked, the Geometric Channel is Bi-Signature


We now state and prove the structural diagnosis of the asymmetry between the two channels of the McGucken Duality. **Theorem 19.5 (Channel Asymmetry).** Under the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, the algebraic-symmetry channel (the Algebraic Channel) is Lorentzian-locked: it admits only the Lorentzian-signature reading. The geometric-propagation channel (the Geometric Channel) is bi-signature: it admits both Lorentzian and Euclidean signature readings, related by the McGucken-Wick rotation $\tau = x_4/c$. The asymmetry is forced by the structural status of the imaginary unit $i$ in $dx_4/dt = ic$: the $i$ is *interior* to the Algebraic Channel (it is the algebraic invariance content of the principle being read) and *exteriorisable* in the Geometric Channel (it can be moved from the interior of the path weight to the exterior coordinate frame via the McGucken-Wick rotation, becoming a real coordinate identification on the real four-manifold).

*Proof in four structural steps.*

*Step 1 (Locate the imaginary unit $i$ in $dx_4/dt = ic$).* The principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ contains a single load-bearing imaginary unit $i$, multiplying the rate $c$. The $i$ is not a notational decoration; it is the algebraic record of $x_4$'s perpendicularity to the three spatial dimensions $x_1, x_2, x_3$ — the foundational geometric fact that the fourth direction of spacetime is not parallel to any spatial direction but is square-rooted-negative against the spatial three-slice. *Step 2 (The $i$ is interior to the Algebraic Channel).* Algebraic Channel reads $dx_4/dt = ic$ as a statement about *invariance*: the rate $ic$ is unchanged under translations, rotations, and Lorentz boosts that respect the McGucken-foliation structure. ## Theorem 19.5.2: Resolution-Content Diagnosis of the McGucken Duality — the Algebraic Channel Mono-Resolution (Continuous), the Geometric Channel Bi-Resolution (Continuous and Discrete); the Planck Length as the Lorentz-Scalar Discreteness Bridge; Dissolution of Weyl's Tile Argument and the Nielsen–Ninomiya Theorem

The answer, established in the proof below in six structural steps, is:

(a) The Algebraic Channel is mono-resolution: it is uniformly continuous, operating on Lie groups whose continuous structure forbids nontrivial discretization without dissolving the group action. ## Theorem 20: The Two-Tier Structural Architecture of Physics


**Theorem (Two-Tier Structural Architecture; cf.\ [MGUnification], Theorem 7.9.4).** Under the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, the foundational content of physics has exactly three tiers, with the McGucken Duality operating identically at the two non-foundational tiers:

- *Tier 0 (foundational principle)*: $dx_4/dt = ic$. The fourth dimension is expanding spherically at the velocity of light at every spacetime event. This is the single physical postulate from which all subsequent content descends.
- *Tier 1 (matter dynamics on the McGucken manifold)*: The behavior of matter degrees of freedom on the (locally fixed or perturbatively small) McGucken-manifold background. Tier 1 admits a Lorentzian–Euclidean signature duality manifesting as:

   - Lorentzian Tier 1 = *Quantum Mechanics*: matter wavefunctions evolve under unitary Schrödinger dynamics, with path-integral phase $\exp(iS/\hbar)$ and operator algebra $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$.

### Three Tiers, Two Signatures, Four Readings

## Theorem 21: Huygens' Principle is the Holographic Principle


**Theorem (Huygens equals Holography; cf.\ [MGUnification], Theorem 7.9.5).** Under the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, Huygens' Principle and the holographic principle of 't~Hooft and Susskind are two formulations of the same geometric fact: the physics of the bulk region enclosed by a McGucken Sphere at time $t + dt$ is fully determined by source data on the 2-dimensional surface of the McGucken Sphere at time $t$. 1. The 2-dimensional surface of the McGucken Sphere at radius $R = ct$ from event $p_0$ has area $A(t) = 4\pi c^2 t^2$ and carries $N_{\mathrm{modes}} = A/\ell_P^2$ independent $x_4$-modes (cf.\ the area-law of Theorem 15).

**In plain language.** The holographic principle of 't~Hooft and Susskind says that the physics of a (d+1)-dimensional region of space is encoded on its d-dimensional boundary. Every event in spacetime is the apex of a McGucken Sphere, and every McGucken Sphere is a holographic screen. The wavefronts that fill the bulk between time $t$ and time $t + dt$ are sourced from the surface of the Sphere at time $t$—this is the standard Huygens statement, and it is also the standard holographic statement. The Bekenstein bound is the count of how many independent Huygens sources can fit on a Planck-scale grid on the Sphere's surface. AdS/CFT works in anti-de Sitter space because the boundary of the McGucken Sphere there lives at conformal infinity, making the dual CFT a well-defined boundary theory. Holography is not special to black holes or to AdS; it is the universal structural content of $dx_4/dt = ic$ at every spacetime event.

### The Undetected Photon: Single-Quantum Refutation of Susskind's Position


The Brownian Hamlet (Theorem 23b below) and the Brownian Iliad–Odyssey (Theorem 23c below) refute Susskind's "information cannot be destroyed" position at the level of many-particle ensembles. A sharper refutation operates at the level of a *single photon*. The single-quantum case sidesteps any rhetorical move that would dismiss thermodynamic-scale arguments as "messy emergent behavior" — the undetected photon is one quantum, propagating at $c$, on a textbook spherical wavefront, with no thermodynamic averaging required. Following the dual-channel structural analysis of [MGSchrodingerSecondLaw], Sections III–IX, we now establish the six theorems that close on Susskind at the single-quantum level.


#### The Undetected-Photon Thought Experiment


A laboratory emits a single photon at time $t = 0$. The photon propagates spherically outward at the speed of light. No detector intercepts it. We ask: what is the probability of detection?

The orthodox unitarian replies: probability is conserved by unitary evolution. The wavefunction $\psi(\mathbf{x}, t)$ evolves according to the (relativistic) Schrödinger equation, and the global integral

$$\int_{\mathbb{R}^3} |\psi(\mathbf{x}, t)|^2 \, d^3x = 1 \tag{23a.1}$$

is preserved for all $t$. The amplitude is "still somewhere"; no probability has been destroyed. the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel unitarity is intact.

But now consider any actual observer's operationally accessible region. Let $\mathcal{R}(t)$ denote the spatial region within the observer's past light cone of the present moment $t$. By the spherical $x_4$-expansion at rate $c$ from every event ([MGGeometry] Def.\ 5.4 (P2); Theorem 3 of the present paper), $\mathcal{R}(t)$ is bounded. The amplitude in the operationally accessible region is

$$P_{\rm accessible}(t) = \int_{\mathcal{R}(t)} |\psi(\mathbf{x}, t)|^2 \, d^3 x. \tag{23a.2}$$

For a freely propagating photon wavefront expanding spherically from the emission event, $P_{\rm accessible}(t)$ is *monotonically decreasing* in $t$ for any observer not at the emission point. After sufficient time, $P_{\rm accessible}(t) \to 0$ for every observer in the universe.

This is not a violation of the Algebraic Channel unitarity. The global integral $\int_{\mathbb{R}^3} |\psi|^2 = 1$ is intact. But the probability of detection — the probability that any actual observer ever interacts with the photon — falls to zero. The amplitude is "still somewhere" only in the formal sense that the integral over a Platonic $\mathbb{R}^3$ remains unity. The single photon supplies a counter-instance to Susskind's "information cannot be destroyed" position at the single-quantum level, without invoking any thermodynamic ensemble.


#### Theorem 23a.1 (Operational/Metaphysical Dichotomy)


**Theorem 23a.1 (Operational/Metaphysical Dichotomy).** Let the orthodox one-content reading of the Schrödinger equation be: $i\hbar\,\partial_t\psi = \hat H\psi$ expresses unitary evolution and unitarity is the entire physical content of the equation. Under this reading, the orthodox unitarian must choose between the following two positions.

*(A) Operational reading.* Probabilities are probabilities of measurement outcomes. The Born rule applies conditional on a detection. An amplitude that never reaches any detector contributes nothing to any actual probability sum. The statement $\int_{\mathbb{R}^3} |\psi|^2 = 1$ is then a formal algebraic property of the wavefunction, not a physical claim about conserved measurement probability. Unitarity, on this reading, is an algebraic property of $U(t)$, not a statement about probabilities of events that never occur.

*(B) Metaphysical reading.* Probabilities are intrinsic to $\psi$ independent of measurement. The global integral $\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}|\psi|^2 = 1$ is a physical claim about amplitude conserved over a Platonic spatial container, irrespective of whether any observer can ever access any part of it. Unitarity, on this reading, is a metaphysical commitment to amplitude bookkeeping on regions no measurement can probe.

Position (A) renders the "unitarity is non-negotiable" defense operationally vacuous for the undetected photon: no operational probability has been violated, because no operational probability was ever computable. Position (B) renders the defense metaphysical: it commits the unitarian to the conservation of a quantity whose only definition is in terms of regions inaccessible to experiment.

*Proof.* By the undetected-photon construction above, $P_{\rm accessible}(t) \to 0$ for every bounded observer while $\int_{\mathbb{R}^3} |\psi|^2 = 1$ is preserved exactly. The orthodox unitarian's claim "probability is conserved by unitary evolution" must therefore be interpreted either in the operational sense (a claim about probabilities of measurement outcomes) or in the metaphysical sense (a claim about a Platonic spatial integral). Under (A), the conservation claim makes no statement about the undetected photon, since the photon produces no measurement outcome at any observer; the defense is vacuous for the case under consideration. Under (B), the conservation claim concerns a quantity defined over regions $\mathbb{R}^3 \setminus \mathcal{R}(t)$ that no observer can probe; the defense is metaphysical. No third interpretation exists within the orthodox one-content reading: any interpretation must either restrict the claim to operationally accessible regions (and become (A)) or extend the claim to operationally inaccessible regions (and become (B)). $\Box$ ∎

*Diagnostic remark.* The orthodox unitarian needs Position (A) to ground the commitment in physics (a science of measurement) and Position (B) to make the commitment universal (applying even to amplitude that no measurement probes). The orthodox one-content reading provides no consistent way to hold both. The undetected photon is the laboratory-bench instance of the black hole information problem: a Hawking quantum emitted from a black hole and propagating to spatial infinity is, modulo cosmological complications, the same object. If the orthodox reading cannot account for the laboratory case without lapsing into metaphysics, it cannot account for the cosmological case either.

#### Theorem 23a.3 (Banks–Peskin–Susskind Rules Out Only the Algebraic Channel Non-Unitarity)


Susskind's central technical support for "unitarity is non-negotiable" rests on the 1984 Banks–Peskin–Susskind theorem [Banks-Peskin-Susskind1984]. It does not rule out, and is silent on, monotonic $+ic$-driven geometric-propagation effects (the Geometric Channel) that leave $U(t)$ unitary while inducing operational information loss via spherical $x_4$-dilution, horizon crossing, or causal-region exit.

Its conclusion is that such an operation propagates to produce observable pathologies (energy non-conservation, vacuum heating, locality violation). ### The Measurement-Problem Dissolution: Four Subproblems as Direct Corollaries


The Schrödinger-contains-Second-Law identity of Theorem 22 dissolves a second foundational problem of quantum mechanics, structurally parallel to the Hawking–Susskind paradox: the orthodox measurement problem, central to QM since the von Neumann 1932 formulation [vonNeumann1932] and unresolved through Copenhagen, Everett 1957, GRW 1986, decoherence (Zeh 1970, Zurek 1981–2005), and the more recent constructive proposals (CSL, Penrose–Diósi, spontaneous-localization variants). The orthodox measurement problem decomposes into four subproblems (MP1)–(MP4); under the McGucken framework, each is dissolved as a direct corollary of published companion theorems.

**(MP1) Preferred-basis selection.** Why does an apparatus settle on the pointer-position basis $\{|A_n\rangle\}$ rather than some superposition basis? Under [Theorem 7.1]MGSchrodingerSecondLaw, the Born density $P = |\psi|^2$ at a measurement event $B$ is the geometric overlap, at $B$, of the forward $x_4$-expansion (carrying phase from $x_4 = +ict$) and the conjugate $x_4^*$-expansion (carrying phase from $x_4^* = -ict$). The apparatus pointer-position basis is the basis of spatial-position eigenstates on which the McGucken Sphere of each apparatus constituent has geometric support. The preferred basis is forced by the McGucken Sphere geometry, not selected by external coupling.

**(MP2) Outcome selection: how does a single outcome emerge from a superposition?** For a gram-scale apparatus of $N \sim 10^{23}$ Compton-coupled constituent spheres, the interaction with a measured quantum system is structurally an $(N+1)$-vertex Feynman vertex where the system's McGucken Sphere intersects pairwise with the apparatus's $N$ Compton-coupled spheres. The $N$-vertex Dyson expansion produces a localization rate

$$\Gamma \;\sim\; N\,\omega_C \;\sim\; 10^{23}\cdot 10^{24}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}} \;\sim\; 10^{47}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}},$$

where $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar \sim 10^{24}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}$ is the Compton frequency of a proton-mass apparatus constituent. The localization is therefore essentially instantaneous at any laboratory timescale: $\Gamma^{-1} \sim 10^{-47}$ s is three orders of magnitude below the Planck time $t_P \sim 5.4\times 10^{-44}$ s, and any apparatus interaction is dynamically localized at the McGucken-Sphere intersection events in vastly less than one Planck time. The branch selected is the one whose system-apparatus intersection event lies on the forward $+ic$ light cone of the preparation event; the suppressed branches dissipate into the apparatus's $N \sim 10^{23}$ Compton-coupled degrees of freedom through the same Compton-coupled Brownian mechanism that dissolves the Brownian Hamlet (Theorem 23). Outcome selection is therefore not a separate non-unitary postulate but a direct consequence of the $(N+1)$-vertex Dyson expansion at any macroscopic measurement event.

**(MP3) Born rule: probabilities $P(\phi_n) = |c_n|^2$.** Under [Theorem 4.2]MGBornRule, the Born rule is the unique density $P:\mathbb{R}^3\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ satisfying four requirements read off the geometric content of $dx_4/dt = ic$: (R1) reality $P\in\mathbb{R}$; (R2) non-negativity $P\ge 0$; (R3) phase invariance under global $x_4$-shift $\psi \to e^{i\alpha}\psi$; (R4) bilinearity in $(\psi, \psi^*)$, with (R4) supplied by the rank-2 character of the Minkowski metric induced by $x_4 = ict$, $(ict)^2 = -c^2 t^2$. The metric pairs two four-velocity vectors and produces a scalar; hence the probability density is bilinear in $(\psi, \psi^*)$. Applied to the joint system-apparatus state $\sum_n c_n |\phi_n\rangle \otimes |A_n\rangle$, the Born density on the pointer-state basis is $P(\phi_n \otimes A_n) = |c_n|^2$. **(MP3$'$) the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel uniqueness theorem for the Born rule.** [11.3, Theorem B.7]MGSchrodingerSecondLaw supplies a structurally-disjoint the Geometric Channel derivation of $P = |\psi|^2$ from the geometric incidence of pairwise McGucken Sphere intersections at measurement events. The Geometric Channel route uses only iterated McGucken Sphere expansion, Huygens wavefronts, Compton-frequency phase accumulation, and the geometric incidence of two expansions at the measurement event — with no algebraic uniqueness argument, no phase-invariance appeal, and no rank-2-metric input. #### Shannon Entropy and the Three-Sector Coincidence


The most pointed near-miss is the Shannon-entropy identity, because Shannon entropy and von Neumann entropy are explicitly defined in terms of the wavefunction/density matrix of the Schrödinger equation, yet the thermodynamic content was not extracted.

Shannon 1948 [Shannon1948] and von Neumann's prior derivation [vonNeumann1932]. Shannon's entropy formula $H = -\sum_i p_i \log p_i$ was, by Shannon's own account in a 1971 interview, suggested to him by John von Neumann. The story: Shannon was looking for a name for his information-theoretic quantity, and von Neumann said "Call it entropy. It's already used in statistical mechanics with the same form, and besides, nobody knows what entropy really is, so in a debate you'll always have the advantage." The Shannon–von Neumann entropy is formally identical to the Boltzmann–Gibbs entropy of statistical mechanics:

$$H_{\mathrm{Shannon}} = -\sum_i p_i \log p_i, \qquad S_{\mathrm{BG}} = -\kB\sum_i p_i \log p_i,$$

up to the Boltzmann constant factor. Von Neumann had already in 1932 [vonNeumann1932] derived the quantum entropy $S_{\rm vN} = -\mathrm{Tr}(\rho \log \rho)$ for density matrices, structurally identical to the Shannon entropy applied to quantum probability distributions.

**The 76-year historical puzzle: documented senior-figure admissions that the entropy identity could not be explained.** The recurrence of the same functional form $-\sum_i p_i \log p_i$ across statistical mechanics (Boltzmann 1872 [Boltzmann1872], Gibbs 1902 [Gibbs1902]), quantum mechanics (von Neumann 1932 [vonNeumann1932]), and information theory (Shannon 1948 [Shannon1948]) was recognized as a structural puzzle from the moment of Shannon's 1948 publication. The puzzle has *not been satisfactorily resolved* in the orthodox literature in the seventy-six years from Shannon 1948 through Lieb–Yngvason 1999 through the present 2026 corpus. The historical record contains a sustained cluster of admissions by senior figures across five decades that the appearance of the same formula in three apparently distinct sectors *cannot be explained* from foundational principles within the orthodox framework. The cluster is structurally parallel to the Huang–Zee–Wolfram–Feynman cluster of admissions about the QM ↔ statistical-mechanics Wick-rotation correspondence documented in the Pre-Wick Genealogy subsection of the present paper; both clusters are residues of the same blind spot — the missing foundational principle that the McGucken framework supplies as $dx_4/dt = ic$.

*The von Neumann admission (1948, transmitted via Shannon to Tribus 1961, published 1971).* The canonical primary-source documentation of the unresolved puzzle is the conversation between John von Neumann and Claude Shannon in 1948, when Shannon was searching for a name for his information-theoretic uncertainty measure. The conversation was recounted by Shannon to Myron Tribus in 1961 and first published by Tribus in 1964 in *Heat Transfer, Thermodynamics and Education: Boelter Anniversary Volume* (McGraw-Hill, ed.\ H.\ A.\ Johnson, p.\ 354), with the canonical second publication in Tribus and McIrvine's 1971 *Scientific American* article "Energy and Information" [TribusMcIrvine1971, *Scientific American* 224, September 1971, pp.\ 178–184]. Shannon's recollection in his own words:

> *"My greatest concern was what to call it. I thought of calling it 'information,' but the word was overly used, so I decided to call it 'uncertainty.' When I discussed it with John von Neumann, he had a better idea. Von Neumann told me, 'You should call it entropy, for two reasons. In the first place your uncertainty function has been used in statistical mechanics under that name, so it already has a name. **In the second place, and more important, nobody knows what entropy really is, so in a debate you will always have the advantage.'"** [Shannon to Tribus 1961, published TribusMcIrvine1971]

The von Neumann admission is structurally diagnostic on three counts. *First*, von Neumann recognized that his own 1932 quantum-mechanical entropy $S_{\rm vN} = -\mathrm{Tr}(\rho \log \rho)$ [vonNeumann1932], Shannon's 1948 information-theoretic entropy $H = -\sum_i p_i \log p_i$, and the Boltzmann–Gibbs statistical-mechanical entropy 1872–1902 [Boltzmann1872, Gibbs1902] were the *same formula*. *Second*, von Neumann — the author of *Mathematische Grundlagen der Quantenmechanik* (1932) and the most mathematically sophisticated foundational physicist of the twentieth century — recorded that *no one understood why the formula was the same across the three sectors*. *Third*, von Neumann's "nobody knows what entropy really is" remark was not casual disparagement but a documented technical admission that the foundational question of *why* the entropy identity held had not been answered by anyone, including himself. The remark dates to 1948 and was reproduced in print by Tribus 1964, Tribus and McIrvine 1971, and subsequently in essentially every history of the entropy concept; it is the canonical primary-source admission of the structural gap.

*The Jaynes epistemological relocation (1957).* Edwin T.\ Jaynes's 1957 *Physical Review* article "Information Theory and Statistical Mechanics" [Jaynes1957a, *Phys. Rev.* 106, 620–630, May 15, 1957] and its 1957 sequel [Jaynes1957b, *Phys. Rev.* 108, 171–190] supplied what became the standard orthodox response to the puzzle: relocation of the entropy identity into Bayesian epistemology. Jaynes wrote: *"Information theory provides a constructive criterion for setting up probability distributions on the basis of partial knowledge, and leads to a type of statistical inference which is called the maximum-entropy estimate. It is the least biased estimate possible on the given information; i.e., it is maximally noncommittal with regard to missing information. If one considers statistical mechanics as a form of statistical inference rather than as a physical theory, it is found that the usual computational rules, starting with the determination of the partition function, are an immediate consequence of the maximum-entropy principle. In the resulting 'subjective statistical mechanics,' the usual rules are thus justified independently of any physical argument, and in particular independently of experimental verification."* [Jaynes1957a, p.\ 620]

The Jaynes position is structurally diagnostic on its own terms. Jaynes did *not* derive the Shannon–Boltzmann–von Neumann identity from a foundational physical principle. He *reframed* the question: rather than asking *why* the same formula appears in three sectors, he proposed treating statistical mechanics as a *form of statistical inference* rather than as physics, with the entropy identity then becoming a tautology of the inference procedure. The cost is that the Second Law becomes a fact about observers and their incomplete information rather than a fact about physical reality. Jaynes was direct about this cost: in his 1957 conclusion he wrote that "whether or not the results agree with experiment, they still represent the best estimates that could have been made on the basis of the information available." The epistemic relocation is the orthodox community's most sustained 51-year response to the entropy puzzle (1957 through the present 2008 *Scientific American* and contemporary textbook tradition), and it explicitly does *not* answer the question von Neumann posed in 1948 — it dissolves the question by reinterpreting statistical mechanics as inference rather than physics. #### The Significance of the Three-Fold Unification of Entropy: Statistical Mechanics, Quantum Mechanics, and Information Theory


The structural significance of the McGucken Entropy Identity is best appreciated by isolating the three classical entropies of physics — the Boltzmann–Gibbs entropy of statistical mechanics (1872, 1902), the von Neumann entropy of quantum mechanics (1932), and the Shannon entropy of information theory (1948) — and examining what it means that the McGucken framework establishes them as three readings of the same underlying geometric quantity. The three-fold unification is the deepest structural identification the framework supplies, with consequences across thermodynamics, foundations of quantum mechanics, foundations of information theory, the philosophy of probability, the philosophy of mind, and the relationship between physics and computation.

The three classical entropy formulas are:

$$
S_{\rm BG} = -\kB \sum_i p_i \ln p_i \quad \text{(Boltzmann–Gibbs, statistical mechanics)},
$$

$$
S_{\rm vN} = -\kB \operatorname{Tr}(\hat{\rho} \ln \hat{\rho}) \quad \text{(von Neumann, quantum mechanics)},
$$

$$
H_{\rm Sh} = -\sum_i p_i \log_2 p_i \quad \text{(Shannon, information theory)}.
$$

The three formulas have *identical functional form* up to a multiplicative constant and the choice of logarithm base. They were derived independently across seventy-six years by three different communities — physicists studying gas thermodynamics, mathematicians studying quantum measurement, and engineers studying communication channels — for three different physical purposes, with three different motivations, and with no structural reason in the orthodox literature for the agreement to be necessary. The orthodox justification has been Shannon's three axioms (continuity, monotonicity, branching), which establish that $-\sum p_i \log p_i$ is the *unique* functional form (up to multiplicative constant) satisfying these axioms for an ignorance-measure. This is a mathematical fact about the functional form; it is *not* a physical fact about why the formula should govern entropy across three independent sectors of physics simultaneously.

The McGucken Entropy Identity supplies the missing physical content. Under $dx_4/dt = ic$, all three formulas read the same underlying quantity — the entropy of the $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-invariant Haar measure on the spatial cross-section of the McGucken Sphere — through three different signature-projections of the same underlying geometry. This subsection works through the structural significance of this unification in eight distinct dimensions.


##### Significance 1: The Shannon–von Neumann Naming Anecdote and Its Resolution


The historical accident that crystallizes the structural mystery is the well-known Shannon–von Neumann naming anecdote. In 1948, Claude Shannon — having derived his information-theoretic formula $H = -\sum_i p_i \log p_i$ for a communication channel — sought a name for the quantity. He consulted John von Neumann, who reportedly advised him: *"You should call it entropy, for two reasons. In the first place your uncertainty function has been used in statistical mechanics under that name, so it already has a name. In the second place, and more important, no one knows what entropy really is, so in a debate you will always have the advantage"* [TribusMcIrvine1971]. Von Neumann's reply — half-joking, half-serious — encodes the structural mystery exactly: the formula was known to appear in statistical mechanics under the name "entropy" yet *nobody understood what entropy was at the foundational level*. The naming was a strategic move precisely because the structural identification was not understood.

The McGucken Entropy Identity supplies the resolution. The reason the formula appears identically in both statistical mechanics and information theory is *not* a coincidence of mathematical form; it is the structural fact that both sectors read the same underlying McGucken-Sphere Haar measure through different signature-projections of $dx_4/dt = ic$. Shannon's "uncertainty function" and Boltzmann's "entropy" are the same physical quantity expressed in two different domains: Boltzmann reads the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel Euclidean signature on the microstate ensemble; Shannon reads the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel Lorentzian signature on the discrete-symbol partition. Both are the geometric content of the McGucken Sphere expressed under the appropriate signature. Von Neumann's quip — that nobody knew what entropy really was — is in retrospect the most honest statement of the field's structural confusion: the three classical entropies were known to share a functional form, but the *physical reason* for the sharing was inaccessible without the active-expansion content of $dx_4/dt = ic$. The McGucken framework supplies the physical reason; the naming becomes structurally well-founded; von Neumann's joke ceases to be an admission of ignorance and becomes a recognition of a deep structural identity that was awaiting articulation.

##### Significance 3: The Resolution of the Objective–Subjective Entropy Dispute


The three-fold appearance of the entropy formula has been the central battleground of a hundred-year dispute in the foundations of statistical mechanics: is entropy *objective* (a physical quantity intrinsic to a system, on the Boltzmann–Gibbs reading) or *subjective* (an observer-dependent measure of ignorance, on the Shannon–Jaynes reading)? The Boltzmann–Gibbs reading treats entropy as a property of the physical microstate ensemble: a gas at temperature $T$ has a definite entropy given by its phase-space distribution, regardless of any observer. The Shannon–Jaynes reading treats entropy as a property of the observer's probability assignment: entropy quantifies the observer's ignorance about which microstate the system is in, given the macroscopic constraints the observer has knowledge of.

The dispute has been irresolvable from inside the orthodox framework because both readings can be defended: the Boltzmann–Gibbs reading is mathematically correct (the formula gives the correct equilibrium thermodynamics); the Shannon–Jaynes reading is mathematically correct (the formula gives the correct maximum-entropy inference under given constraints). The two readings agree numerically; the dispute is about the *physical interpretation* of the agreement.

The McGucken Entropy Identity resolves the dispute by establishing that *both readings are correct and they refer to two channels of the same underlying physical structure*. The Boltzmann–Gibbs reading is the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel Euclidean signature-projection of the McGucken-Sphere Haar measure onto the microstate ensemble; the Shannon–Jaynes reading is the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel Lorentzian signature-projection of the same Haar measure onto the observer's probability assignment. Both projections descend from the same underlying geometric quantity (the McGucken-Sphere Haar measure under Compton-coupling matter-interaction), and the equality of their numerical values is a direct consequence of their shared source. The objective–subjective dispute dissolves: the entropy is objective at the Geometric Channel level (the McGucken-Sphere geometry is real at every spacetime event), and the same entropy is also expressible at the Algebraic Channel level as the observer's ignorance-measure, with the numerical agreement being the dual-channel signature of the underlying geometry. Both Boltzmann and Jaynes were right; the orthodox framework lacked the structural language to identify what they were *jointly* right about.

#### Constructor Theory as the Most Recent Near-Miss: Deutsch–Marletto 2013–2025


The Cascade of Near-Misses extends into the present decade. The most recent significant addition is the constructor-theoretic program of David Deutsch and Chiara Marletto: the foundational *constructor theory* [Deutsch2013], the *constructor theory of information* [DeutschMarletto2015], and the *constructor theory of thermodynamics* [Marletto2016]. The program operates from Oxford's Materials Department and Centre for Quantum Computation and has produced a sustained research output, including experimental quantum-simulation work establishing irreversible processes at the quantum scale [MarlettoVedraltal2020]. The constructor-theoretic program makes the explicit claim that the first and second laws of thermodynamics carry information-theoretic content, with the connection to information not limited to the second law (as in Landauer 1961 and Bennett 1973) but extending to the first law as well. This subsection establishes the precise structural relationship between the constructor-theoretic program and the McGucken framework: *constructor theory is the most recent surfacing of the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel without the active-expansion content of $dx_4/dt = ic$, and constructor theory's five distinct structural insights are five direct theorems of the McGucken framework with the foundational physical mechanism supplied.*


**The constructor-theoretic claim.**
 Deutsch and Marletto invert the standard formulation of physical laws. Rather than "given initial conditions and dynamical laws, predict trajectories," they ask: "which physical transformations admit a constructor capable of performing them reliably and repeatedly?" A *task* is a specification of an input-output transformation; a task is *possible* if a constructor for it can exist with arbitrarily high accuracy and reliability under the laws of physics, and *impossible* if no such constructor can exist. The laws of physics are reformulated as statements about which tasks are possible and which are impossible [Deutsch2013]. Marletto's 2016 constructor theory of thermodynamics applies this framework to the laws of thermodynamics, introducing a scale-independent constructor-theoretic notion of *adiabatic accessibility* via *work media* (substrates whose energy-storage variables generalize the "weight in a gravitational field" of standard adiabatic-accessibility definitions). The constructor-theoretic second law states that certain physical states are adiabatically inaccessible from one another — there exists no constructor for the inverse transformation. The first law is reformulated as the requirement that work media be *interoperable* — all ways of doing work on a substrate must agree at the level of net energy transfer. The information-theoretic connection emerges from the requirement that work media be physically realizable substrates carrying information about energy stored.


**The constructor-theoretic information program.**
 The 2015 *constructor theory of information* [DeutschMarletto2015] expresses information theory in constructor-theoretic terms: classical information is the substrate on which certain copying tasks are possible; quantum information ("superinformation") is the substrate on which the copying task is impossible but other tasks remain possible. This program explicitly rejects the Wheeler 1989 "It from Bit" proposition of information as the fundamental substance of physics [Wheeler1989] on technical grounds: Wheeler's program treats information as an *a priori* mathematical or logical concept, leading to circularity (information and distinguishability are each defined in terms of the other). Deutsch–Marletto reverse the direction: the nature and laws of information *follow from* the laws of physics rather than constituting them. This is structurally an advance on the Wheeler program, but as we shall establish in (D5) below, it leaves the deeper question — which laws of physics give rise to the information-theoretic content of thermodynamics — unanswered.

 We catalog five distinct structural points where constructor theory's content is genuinely a partial reading of the Geometric Channel of $dx_4/dt = ic$ without the active-expansion mechanism.

Marletto's work/heat distinction at the constructor-theoretic level is the operational expression of the McGucken Duality of $dx_4/dt = ic$ at the energy-transfer level; the McGucken framework supplies the structural origin (the Geometric Channel is geometric-propagation; the Algebraic Channel is algebraic-symmetry; the work/heat distinction is the operational shadow of the channel split at the energy-transfer level).

 Constructor theory's explicit positioning against Wheeler's 1989 "It from Bit" program [Wheeler1989] merits structural comment.  Constructor theory is a real program by serious physicists at Oxford who have noticed something genuinely important: the laws of thermodynamics carry information-theoretic content, and not only the second law (which Landauer 1961 already established) but the first law too.
