### §28.2 The Master Diagnostic: The Unitarity-versus-Randomness Contradiction


The cleanest single illustration of the orthodox postulate-accumulation pattern in foundational thermodynamics is the **unitarity-versus-randomness contradiction**. The contradiction is on the surface of every standard textbook of statistical mechanics, of quantum mechanics, and of quantum field theory. It is enunciated in the public lectures of every prominent foundational physicist of the past half-century. And it is treated by the orthodox community as a feature rather than a bug.

**The two orthodox claims.** The orthodox foundational position rests on two claims that are advanced simultaneously, often in the same paper and sometimes in the same paragraph:

*Claim A (Unitarity).* Quantum mechanics is strictly unitary. The Schrödinger evolution $\hat U(t) = \exp(-i\hat H t/\hbar)$ is a unitary representation of the time-translation group, preserves the inner product on Hilbert space, is time-reversible, and conserves information (no information is destroyed by Schrödinger evolution; the von Neumann entropy of the universe-wide quantum state is exactly preserved). Black-hole information conservation, the gravitational path integral, and the AdS/CFT correspondence are all built on this unitarity claim.

*Claim B (Randomness).* Random fluctuations, thermal noise, stochastic forcings, and probabilistic outcomes are ubiquitous in physical reality. Brownian motion is genuinely stochastic. Thermal noise in resistors is genuinely random. Classical chaos amplifies initial-condition uncertainty to produce apparent randomness. Quantum measurements have genuinely probabilistic outcomes. Quantum fluctuations populate the vacuum.

**The contradiction.** Claims A and B cannot both be true under the orthodox framework as it stands. If Claim A is correct — quantum mechanics is strictly unitary — then every physical phenomenon that ultimately reduces to quantum-mechanical evolution is itself unitary, deterministic, and time-reversible. Thermal noise in a resistor is the macroscopic signature of quantum-mechanical fluctuations of electrons coupled to phonon modes; under strict unitarity, those fluctuations are themselves unitary. There is no randomness *in principle* — only randomness *in practice* arising from ignorance of the exact microscopic state. The same applies to Brownian motion, to classical chaos initial-condition uncertainty, and to vacuum fluctuations: all are quantum-mechanical at their substrate, all are unitary under Claim A, none are *fundamentally* random.

If randomness is genuinely real anywhere in physics, then unitarity is not exact. If unitarity is exact, then randomness is at best an epistemic illusion arising from ignorance of microscopic state. The orthodox framework refuses to commit to either horn. In the same paper, in the same paragraph, sometimes in the same sentence, both claims are advanced.

**The handwaving sources of randomness.** When pressed on the source of randomness in thermodynamics, the orthodox framework retreats to handwaves that are themselves forbidden by the unitarity story:

- *"Thermal noise."* Thermal noise in resistors, in semiconductors, in Brownian-motion observations is a quantum-mechanical phenomenon at its substrate. Under strict unitarity, thermal noise is deterministic and time-reversible at the microscopic level. The handwave smuggles in randomness from outside the unitary substrate.

- *"Quantum fluctuations."* Vacuum fluctuations in quantum field theory are formal artifacts of the quantization procedure on a unitary Hilbert space. The vacuum state $|0\rangle$ is an eigenstate of the Hamiltonian and evolves trivially. The handwave smuggles in "fluctuations" that are inconsistent with the eigenstate structure.

- *"Decoherence."* Decoherence by an environment produces an effectively diagonal reduced density matrix on the system, but the global system-plus-environment evolution is unitary; the diagonal structure is only apparent on the reduced state, not the full state. Decoherence does not produce randomness *in principle*; it produces randomness *in practice*, through the unobservability of the environment's degrees of freedom.

- *"Initial-condition uncertainty in chaos theory."* Classical chaos is technically deterministic; apparent randomness arises from sensitive dependence on initial conditions, amplified through positive Lyapunov exponents (§28.3 below). But the initial-condition uncertainty itself must come from somewhere. The handwave to "quantum fluctuations at the molecular scale" or "thermal noise" recurs to one of the prior handwaves, which are themselves forbidden by the unitarity story.

The handwaves form a closed loop. Randomness in chaos is sourced from thermal noise; thermal noise is sourced from quantum fluctuations; quantum fluctuations are sourced from the formal structure of QFT — which is unitary, deterministic, and provides no source of randomness. The loop closes without ever providing a foundational source of the randomness that is everywhere observed.

**The McGucken resolution.** The McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ dissolves the unitarity-versus-randomness contradiction at the foundational level by recognizing that *both halves are simultaneously valid* as dual readings of the same source.

*Unitarity of Schrödinger evolution* (Claim A) is the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel content. It is exact on the algebraic-symmetry side of the McGucken duality. The $-i\hbar\partial_t\psi = \hat H\psi$ Schrödinger equation is the matter-tier integrated form of $dx_4/dt = ic$ read through Stone's theorem on the time-translation generator (Theorem 22 of the present paper).

*Randomness in thermal noise, Brownian motion, classical chaos initial-condition uncertainty, and vacuum fluctuations* (Claim B) is the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel content. It is exact on the geometric-propagation side of the McGucken duality. The $+ic$ orientation of $x_4$'s expansion at every event sources matter-tier isotropic random-walk displacement via the Compton coupling (Theorem 4 of the present paper); the McGucken Sphere's spherical expansion at the matter tier IS the random-walk substrate from which thermal noise, Brownian motion, and the classical-chaos initial-condition uncertainty descend.

*The Wick rotation* $\tau = x_4/c$ is the structural bridge between the two channels [MGWickMcWick, Theorem 30.9.2]. Under the McGucken-Wick rotation, the Algebraic Channel's unitary $\hat U(t) = \exp(-i\hat H t/\hbar)$ becomes the Geometric Channel's thermal exponential $\exp(-\tau\hat H/\hbar)$, identified with $\exp(-\beta\hat H/\hbar)$ via the Euclidean-periodicity-equals-inverse-temperature relation $\beta = \tau$. The two channels are *Wick-conjugates* of each other; their simultaneous validity is the structural content of the McGucken duality.

The orthodox contradiction is therefore *not a contradiction at all* in the McGucken framework. It is the duality-blindness of orthodox physics that sees only one side of the McGucken duality at a time and is forced to handwave the other side from somewhere external. The McGucken framework supplies both sides from a single source. The strict Second Law of Theorem 9 of the present paper is the immediate empirical content of this resolution: $dS/dt = (3/2)\kB/t > 0$ is derived through *both* Algebraic Channel (Lindeberg–Lévy CLT + Boltzmann–Gibbs entropy of a Gaussian) and the Geometric Channel (McGucken Sphere volume monotonicity), with the convergence on the same coefficient $3/2$ and the same strict positivity being the structural-overdetermination diagnostic that the McGucken Duality is correctly recognizing what the orthodox framework cannot see.


### §28.3 Postulate: Initial-Condition Uncertainty in Classical Chaos


**What is postulated.** Classical chaos theory was launched by Edward Lorenz's 1963 paper *Deterministic Nonperiodic Flow* (*Journal of the Atmospheric Sciences* **20** (2), 130–141), which demonstrated that a three-variable deterministic ODE system (the Lorenz equations, modeling thermal convection) exhibits sensitive dependence on initial conditions: infinitesimal differences in initial conditions are amplified exponentially in time, with positive Lyapunov exponent $\lambda \approx 0.906$ for the standard Lorenz parameters. The trajectory of the system is *technically deterministic* — given exact initial conditions, the future is uniquely determined — but in practice unpredictable because initial conditions cannot be specified with infinite precision.

The framework was extended by Stephen Smale's horseshoe map (1967), Sinai's billiards (1970), and Ruelle and Takens's strange-attractor theory (1971). In each case, the underlying dynamics is *deterministic* — a Hamiltonian flow, a symplectic map, a smooth diffeomorphism — and the apparent randomness arises *exclusively* from sensitive dependence on initial conditions.

The structural postulate of classical chaos theory is therefore: *initial conditions cannot be specified with infinite precision, and the resulting uncertainty is amplified through positive Lyapunov exponents to produce apparent randomness*.

**What impasse this addresses.** Classical chaos theory addresses the impasse: *how can deterministic classical mechanics produce the apparent randomness observed in real-world thermodynamic systems like weather, fluid turbulence, Brownian motion, and the molecular-scale stochastic forcings that drive macroscopic statistical mechanics?* The framework's answer is that the apparent randomness arises from initial-condition uncertainty rather than from genuinely random dynamics.

**The ontological cost.** The cost of the initial-condition-uncertainty postulate is twofold. *First*, the uncertainty must come from somewhere. If classical mechanics is deterministic and the universe is closed, the initial-condition uncertainty of any subsystem must arise from coupling to a larger system whose state is in turn unknown. The chain terminates at the universal initial condition — which, under classical mechanics, is a definite point in phase space. There is no source of fundamental uncertainty within a closed classical-mechanical universe. The handwave is to invoke "quantum fluctuations" or "thermal noise" as the source of the molecular-scale uncertainty that gets amplified through chaos — but as established in §28.2, these sources are themselves handwaves within the orthodox unitarity story. *Second*, the framework cannot distinguish epistemic from ontological randomness. In a strictly deterministic universe, all randomness is epistemic — arising from observer ignorance rather than from underlying dynamics. The framework treats epistemic randomness as if it were the same as ontological randomness for predictive purposes; this works in practice but is structurally incoherent.

**The McGucken source.** The McGucken framework's the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel supplies the randomness in chaos theory as a structural feature of the matter-tier diffusion driven by $x_4$'s spherical expansion, with no need for initial-condition uncertainty as a separate postulate.

The mechanism: every matter-tier particle is Compton-coupled to $x_4$ at the Compton frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ (Theorem 4 of the present paper). The Compton coupling sources isotropic random-walk displacement at every Compton-frequency tick, producing a matter-tier diffusion process with mean-squared displacement growing as $\langle|\Delta x|^2\rangle = 6Dt$ where $D = \hbar/(2m)$ for a free particle. The diffusion is *not* sourced from initial-condition uncertainty — it is sourced from the geometric content of $x_4$'s spherical expansion at $+ic$ acting on every Compton-coupled particle at every event. The Lorenz-equation thermal convection, the Smale horseshoe, the Sinai billiards, and the strange attractors of Ruelle–Takens are then *macroscopic amplifications* of this matter-tier Compton-coupled randomness, not amplifications of a hand-postulated initial-condition uncertainty. The matter-tier randomness is the foundational input; chaos theory's sensitive dependence is the amplification mechanism that makes the matter-tier randomness visible at macroscopic scale.

The randomness in classical chaos is therefore not a handwave to something external; it is a derived consequence of $dx_4/dt = ic$ acting on Compton-coupled matter at every event. the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel's deterministic Hamiltonian flow remains exact at the algebraic-symmetry level; the Geometric Channel's matter-tier random-walk diffusion is the geometric-propagation content of the same source. Both are valid simultaneously. The numerical confirmation of the Geometric Channel's matter-tier diffusion is supplied in primary-source form by the five-trial mean-squared-displacement simulation of [MGJacobson2026Mechanism §III.1], which Theorem 9 of the present paper incorporates as the third structurally disjoint route (alongside the Algebraic Channel CLT-based analytic route and the Geometric Channel Sphere-volume-monotonicity analytic route) confirming the strict positivity $dS/dt > 0$.

### §28.4 Postulate: Boltzmann's Stosszahlansatz of Molecular Chaos


**What is postulated.** Ludwig Boltzmann's 1872 derivation of the H-theorem (*Weitere Studien über das Wärmegleichgewicht unter Gasmolekülen*, *Sitzungsberichte der kaiserlichen Akademie der Wissenschaften* **66**, 275–370) requires a structural assumption that has become known as the *Stosszahlansatz* (German for "collision number ansatz") or *molecular chaos assumption*: the velocities of two molecules about to collide are *statistically independent* before the collision. After the collision, they may be (and generally are) statistically correlated through the collision dynamics; but before the collision, the joint two-particle distribution $f_2(\mathbf{v}_1, \mathbf{v}_2)$ factorizes as $f_2(\mathbf{v}_1, \mathbf{v}_2) = f_1(\mathbf{v}_1) f_1(\mathbf{v}_2)$.

The Stosszahlansatz is the time-asymmetric input from which Boltzmann derives the time-asymmetric H-theorem: $dH/dt \leq 0$ for $H = \int f \ln f\, d^3v$, with equality if and only if $f$ is Maxwell–Boltzmann. The H-theorem then implies the strict Second Law.

**What impasse this addresses.** Boltzmann's framework addresses the impasse: *how does the strict Second Law (entropy increase) emerge from time-reversible Newtonian molecular dynamics?* Boltzmann's answer was the Stosszahlansatz — but the answer was immediately attacked by Loschmidt 1876 (the reversibility objection: if the molecular dynamics is time-reversible, why isn't the entropy-decreasing direction equally likely?) and by Zermelo 1896 (the recurrence objection: the Poincaré recurrence theorem implies that any closed Hamiltonian system returns arbitrarily close to its initial state, contradicting strict monotonic entropy growth). Boltzmann's response to these objections was to introduce a further postulate: the universe began in a *low-entropy initial state*, and we are observing the relaxation toward equilibrium from that improbable initial condition. The strict Second Law holds *because of the low-entropy initial condition*, not because of any underlying time-asymmetry in the molecular dynamics.

**The ontological cost.** The Stosszahlansatz and its supporting low-entropy initial condition carry three distinct costs.

*Cost 1: time-asymmetric input for time-asymmetric output.* The Stosszahlansatz assumes statistical independence *before* collisions but not *after*. This is a *time-asymmetric* assumption that is structurally identical to the asymmetric result it derives. The H-theorem is therefore not a derivation of the Second Law from time-symmetric dynamics; it is a tautology that derives a time-asymmetric result from a time-asymmetric input. *Cost 2: the low-entropy initial condition is itself unexplained.* If the universe began in a low-entropy state, *why* did it begin in a low-entropy state? The orthodox framework supplies no answer. Boltzmann himself oscillated between two responses: the low-entropy state was a rare statistical fluctuation in an otherwise equilibrium universe (the *fluctuation hypothesis*), or the low-entropy state is just brute fact about cosmological initial conditions. Both responses are unsatisfactory: the fluctuation hypothesis is demolished by the *Boltzmann brain* reductio (it is overwhelmingly more probable to fluctuate directly to a brain experiencing the present moment than to fluctuate to a low-entropy state from which 13.8 Gyr of evolution then produces a brain); the brute-fact response is the explicit abdication of an explanation. *Cost 3: the Stosszahlansatz fails at sufficiently long time-scales.* Even with the low-entropy initial condition, the Stosszahlansatz holds only for a finite time-window; eventually, Poincaré recurrence brings the system arbitrarily close to its initial state, at which point entropy must *decrease*. The orthodox framework handwaves this by asserting that Poincaré recurrence times are "astronomically long" — but the structural issue is that the framework predicts strict $dS/dt \geq 0$ for finite times and strict $dS/dt = 0$ on average over Poincaré recurrence, which is internally inconsistent.

**The McGucken source.** The McGucken framework's the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel supplies the strict Second Law as a *direct* consequence of $x_4$'s $+ic$ orientation, with no Stosszahlansatz, no low-entropy initial condition, and no time-asymmetric input.

The mechanism is Theorem 9 of the present paper, which derives $dS/dt = (3/2)\kB/t > 0$ via two structurally disjoint routes. *$dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel* (algebraic-symmetry): ISO(3)-invariant Gaussian distribution + Lindeberg–Lévy Central Limit Theorem applied to Compton-coupled isotropic random displacements + Boltzmann–Gibbs entropy of a Gaussian giving $S(t) = (3\kB/2)\ln(2\pi e Dt) + \text{const}$, hence $dS/dt = (3/2)\kB/t > 0$. *Geometric Channel* (geometric-propagation): McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(p)$ at every event $p$ has spherically symmetric volume monotonically growing as $V(\Sigma_+(p, t)) = (4\pi/3)(ct)^3$ under $x_4$'s expansion at $+ic$. The matter-tier ensemble's mean-squared displacement grows monotonically with the Sphere's volume; the Boltzmann–Gibbs entropy then grows as $(3\kB/2)\ln V \propto (3\kB/2)\ln t$, hence $dS/dt = (3/2)\kB/t > 0$.

The two channels share no intermediate machinery; their convergence on the same coefficient $3/2$, the same dependence $1/t$, and the same strict positivity is the dual-channel Kleinian-correspondence diagnostic. The strict Second Law is therefore *not* an emergent statistical regularity derived from a time-asymmetric Stosszahlansatz; it is a geometric theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$, derived without any time-asymmetric input. The time-asymmetry is *in the source* (the $+ic$ orientation of $x_4$'s expansion has no $-ic$ counterpart, Theorem 11 of the present paper); the time-asymmetry of the conclusion is therefore not an extra assumption but a derived consequence of the time-asymmetry of the principle.

Theorem 12 of the present paper makes the structural dissolution of Loschmidt's paradox explicit: the reversibility objection is dissolved because $dx_4/dt = ic$ supplies a unidirectional orientation that is not present in the time-symmetric Hamiltonian dynamics Loschmidt was assuming. Loschmidt's argument is *correct* about Newtonian molecular dynamics — and the McGucken framework agrees that Algebraic Channel's unitary evolution is time-symmetric. But the Geometric Channel's geometric-propagation content has the $+ic$ orientation that no $-ic$ counterpart can offset, supplying the arrow that Loschmidt's time-symmetric substrate cannot. The Boltzmann–Loschmidt–Zermelo paradox is dissolved at the structural level: the strict Second Law is derived via two independent channels, without any time-asymmetric input, without any low-entropy initial condition, without any Stosszahlansatz, and without any Poincaré-recurrence escape clause. The Poincaré recurrence itself dissolves: $x_4$'s active expansion at every event means the McGucken Sphere is *not* a closed system on which Poincaré recurrence applies; the expansion of $x_4$ supplies an open structural escape from the closed-system assumption Poincaré requires.

### §28.5 Postulate: The Past Hypothesis of Albert–Loewer–Carroll


**What is postulated.** The *Past Hypothesis* — David Albert's 2000 *Time and Chance* (Harvard University Press) and Barry Loewer's 2007 *Counterfactuals and the Second Law* — is the explicit postulate that the universe began in a low-entropy initial state. The hypothesis is added to the orthodox statistical-mechanical framework to address the structural issue identified in §28.4: that Boltzmann's H-theorem requires a low-entropy initial condition without providing one.

The Past Hypothesis treats the low-entropy initial state as a *brute fact about cosmological initial conditions* — a constraint on the universal wavefunction or on the cosmological phase-space measure that is not derived from anything more fundamental. The Second Law follows from the Past Hypothesis plus statistical-mechanical reasoning: starting from a low-entropy state, the overwhelming majority of microstates compatible with the macroscopic constraints have higher entropy than the initial state, so the system evolves toward higher entropy with overwhelming probability. The Past Hypothesis has been promoted to the status of a *cosmological law* by Albert, Loewer, and Sean Carroll. Carroll's 2010 book *From Eternity to Here: The Quest for the Ultimate Theory of Time* (Dutton) is a sustained advocacy of the Past Hypothesis as the foundational explanation of the arrow of time.

**What impasse this addresses.** The Past Hypothesis addresses the impasse: *why is the entropy of the universe so much lower in the past than in the future, given that classical statistical mechanics is time-symmetric?* The orthodox framework treats this as a question about *initial conditions*: the dynamics are symmetric, but the initial state is special. The Past Hypothesis is the brute-fact assertion that the initial state was special.

**The ontological cost.** The Past Hypothesis carries four distinct costs.

*Cost 1: it is brute fact without further explanation.* The Past Hypothesis is not derived from anything — it is an additional axiom of cosmology, added to the existing axioms of statistical mechanics. Roger Penrose's Weyl-curvature hypothesis (*Singularities and time-asymmetry*, in *General Relativity: An Einstein Centenary Survey*, ed.\ Hawking and Israel, Cambridge University Press, 1979, pp.\ 581–638) attempts to motivate the low-entropy initial condition geometrically through the conformal-curvature structure of the initial singularity, but the motivation requires the Weyl curvature to vanish at past singularities and grow toward future singularities — which is itself an additional postulate beyond standard general relativity.

*Cost 2: it explains the arrow of time only "near" the initial state.* The Past Hypothesis gives a low-entropy state at $t = 0$. The Second Law then follows for short times after $t = 0$ as the system relaxes toward equilibrium. But for very long times (much greater than the Poincaré recurrence time of the universe), the system returns arbitrarily close to its initial state and the Second Law fails. The Past Hypothesis is therefore not a *fundamental* explanation of the arrow of time; it is a *local-in-time* explanation that breaks down at sufficiently long time-scales.

*Cost 3: it does not explain why the thermodynamic arrow aligns with the cosmological, radiative, causal, and psychological-memory arrows.* The Past Hypothesis explains the thermodynamic arrow as a relaxation from a low-entropy initial state. It does not explain why electromagnetic radiation is emitted outward rather than absorbed inward (the radiative arrow), why the universe is expanding rather than contracting (the cosmological arrow), why causes precede effects (the causal arrow), or why we remember the past rather than the future (the psychological arrow). These four additional arrows of time are *separately* postulated in the orthodox framework, each with its own structural assumptions.

*Cost 4: the Boltzmann brain reductio.* If the Past Hypothesis is the brute-fact source of the low-entropy state, and statistical mechanics plus the laws of physics plus 13.8 Gyr of evolution are required to produce a brain experiencing the present moment from the initial low-entropy state, then it is overwhelmingly more probable for a brain to spontaneously fluctuate into existence directly from equilibrium than for the entire 13.8 Gyr evolutionary path to produce one. The Past Hypothesis as a *typical* low-entropy state therefore makes the existence of structured observers exponentially less likely than the existence of fluctuated Boltzmann brains. The orthodox response is either to deny the calculation or to add further postulates (the *typicality* requirement of Albert; the *Carroll–Chen multiverse* of 2004 in which a time-symmetric multiverse has both entropy-increasing and entropy-decreasing branches, with structured observers in the entropy-increasing direction). Each adds another layer of postulation.

**The McGucken source.** Theorem 11 of the present paper supplies the unification of all five arrows of time from a single source — the $+ic$ orientation of $x_4$'s expansion at every event — without requiring a low-entropy initial condition.

The mechanism: $x_4$'s expansion at $+ic$ is *unidirectional* and *spherically symmetric* at every event. The five arrows are five projections of this single fact. *Thermodynamic arrow*: the McGucken Sphere's volume monotonically increases at every event under $x_4$'s expansion; the matter-tier random-walk has positive mean-squared displacement; entropy increases (Theorems 9, 9b, 11). *Radiative arrow*: electromagnetic radiation propagates outward on the future McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(p)$ rather than inward on the past sphere $\Sigma_-(p)$ because $+ic$ orientation forces the retarded Green's function as the physical-propagation kernel. *Cosmological arrow*: the universe expands rather than contracts because the cosmic-scale McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+^{\rm cosmo}$ is the universal McGucken Sphere of the universe-as-event, expanding at $+ic$. The Hubble expansion is the cosmological-scale projection of $x_4$'s expansion (Theorem 18). *Causal arrow*: causes precede effects because the future McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(p)$ is the unique surface to which information can causally propagate from $p$; the past sphere $\Sigma_-(p)$ is the past surface from which information has arrived at $p$, not a surface to which information can be sent. *Psychological arrow*: memory traces accumulate forward in time because memory-encoding in neural systems is a Compton-coupled thermodynamic process subject to the matter-tier strict Second Law; the brain's entropy grows forward in time with the rest of the universe.

All five arrows are *parallel projections* of $+ic$ orientation at every event. None requires a low-entropy initial condition. The Past Hypothesis is dissolved at the structural level: the arrow is *not* a property of an initial state; it is a property of $x_4$'s *current* expansion at every event. The Boltzmann brain reductio dissolves: a Boltzmann brain cannot fluctuate from equilibrium because the McGucken framework has no equilibrium to fluctuate from — the matter-tier random-walk has $+ic$ orientation and no $-ic$ counterpart, making downward entropy fluctuations of the required magnitude structurally impossible. The Penrose Weyl-curvature hypothesis dissolves: the geometric content the hypothesis attempts to supply (a vanishing Weyl curvature at past singularities) is recovered as a structural feature of the cosmic-scale McGucken Sphere's spherically symmetric expansion, without requiring the hypothesis as a separate postulate. The Carroll–Chen multiverse dissolves: the McGucken framework has no equilibrium past from which a time-symmetric multiverse could be constructed; the multiverse is superfluous because the Past Hypothesis it was meant to address has itself been dissolved.

### §28.6 Postulate: The Thermal Time Hypothesis of Connes–Rovelli


**What is postulated.** Alain Connes and Carlo Rovelli, in their 1994 paper *Von Neumann algebra automorphisms and time-thermodynamics relation in generally covariant quantum theories* (*Classical and Quantum Gravity* **11**, 2899–2917), proposed the *Thermal Time Hypothesis*: in the absence of a preferred time, time *emerges* from the modular flow of a thermal state via the Tomita–Takesaki theorem.

The mechanism: given a state $\rho$ on a von Neumann algebra $\mathcal{A}$, the Tomita–Takesaki theorem associates a one-parameter automorphism group $\sigma_t^\rho$ of $\mathcal{A}$ — the *modular flow* of the state. If $\rho$ is a thermal state with inverse temperature $\beta$, the modular flow is identified with the time evolution at temperature $T = 1/(\kB\beta)$. Time, on the Thermal Time Hypothesis, is *derived* from the thermal state of the universe rather than postulated as a foundational parameter.

**What impasse this addresses.** The Thermal Time Hypothesis addresses the impasse: *in a generally covariant theory (such as general relativity, in which the diffeomorphism gauge symmetry erases any preferred time), how does time emerge?* Connes–Rovelli's answer: time is not foundational; it emerges from the modular flow of the universal thermal state via the Tomita–Takesaki theorem.

**The ontological cost.** The Thermal Time Hypothesis carries three distinct costs.

*Cost 1: it inverts the orthodox order of thermodynamics-and-time.* In orthodox statistical mechanics, time is foundational and thermodynamics is derived from time-evolution of a many-body system. The thermal-time hypothesis reverses this: thermodynamics is foundational and time is derived from the thermal state. The reversal is structurally non-trivial — the orthodox derivation chain (Hamiltonian dynamics $\to$ microcanonical ensemble $\to$ canonical ensemble $\to$ temperature) is now read backwards (canonical ensemble $\to$ modular flow $\to$ time).

*Cost 2: it requires the universe to be in a thermal state.* The hypothesis only works if the relevant state is thermal — has a well-defined inverse temperature $\beta$ and satisfies the KMS condition. The universe-as-a-whole is *not* in a global thermal state (the cosmological expansion is far from equilibrium, the matter and radiation are at different temperatures, the gravitational degrees of freedom are not in thermal equilibrium with the matter). The thermal-time hypothesis therefore applies only to *local* approximations to the universal state, with the global time emerging from gluing together local modular flows — which has not been worked out in detail.

*Cost 3: the link between modular time and physical time requires identification.* The modular flow $\sigma_t^\rho$ is a one-parameter automorphism of the operator algebra; its identification with *physical* time (the time observers measure with clocks) requires an additional postulate that the modular flow generated by the universal state is indeed the time that observers measure. This identification is, in the orthodox framework, by fiat.

**The McGucken source.** The McGucken framework supplies time as the *integrated coordinate label* of $x_4$'s active expansion — derived from $dx_4/dt = ic$ — without requiring a thermal-state-derived emergence.

The mechanism: $dx_4/dt = ic$ asserts that the fourth dimension expands at rate $c$ in the $+ic$ direction at every event. The integrated coordinate $x_4 = ict$ is therefore the *recorded path* of $x_4$'s expansion through the laboratory's reference frame; the time $t = -ix_4/c$ is the *parameter* of the expansion. Time is not foundational in the sense of being a postulate of the framework; it is *derived* from the kinematics of $x_4$'s expansion. But the derivation is from the *active geometric content* of $x_4$'s expansion, not from a thermal state.

The McGucken framework's relationship to the Thermal Time Hypothesis is structurally interesting and worth making explicit. *Both frameworks derive time from a more foundational structure.* Connes–Rovelli derive time from a thermal state's modular flow; McGucken derives time from $x_4$'s active expansion. *The McGucken derivation is kinematic; the Connes–Rovelli derivation is thermodynamic.* The kinematic derivation supplies time at *every* event (since $x_4$ expands at every event); the thermodynamic derivation supplies time only where there is a thermal state to generate modular flow. *The McGucken framework supplies the thermal state as a derived consequence of $x_4$'s expansion.* Theorem 22 of the present paper establishes that Schrödinger's asymmetry exalts the Second Law, and Theorem 11 supplies the unification of the five arrows. The thermal state of the universe is then a *consequence* of $x_4$'s expansion at $+ic$ acting on the matter-tier ensemble — *not* a foundational input. Connes–Rovelli derive time from the thermal state; McGucken derives the thermal state from $x_4$'s expansion, and time as the integrated coordinate of the same expansion.

The structural relationship is therefore: *Connes–Rovelli is recovered as a $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel Wick-rotated reading of $dx_4/dt = ic$ at the matter tier*. Under the McGucken-Wick rotation $\tau = x_4/c$ [MGWickMcWick, Theorem 30.9.2], the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel's unitary $\hat U(t) = \exp(-i\hat H t/\hbar)$ becomes the Geometric Channel's thermal $\exp(-\beta\hat H/\hbar)$, with $\beta$ identified with $\tau/\hbar$ via the cigar-period identification. The modular flow generated by the thermal state is then the Wick-rotated unitary time-translation, with the McGucken-Wick rotation $\tau = x_4/c$ as the structural bridge. The Tomita–Takesaki modular flow is *not* an alternative derivation of time but the *Geometric Channel Wick-rotated reading* of the same the Algebraic Channel time-translation generator. Both readings are valid simultaneously; neither is the foundational source. The foundational source is $dx_4/dt = ic$.

The Connes–Rovelli program is therefore recognized in the McGucken framework not as a *competitor* but as a *partial recognition* of the McGucken Duality that $dx_4/dt = ic$ makes complete. Connes–Rovelli saw correctly that time and thermodynamics are structurally related at a deep level; they did not see that *both* are dual readings of the same upstream source. The McGucken framework supplies that source.

### §28.7 Summary: The Postulate-Accumulation Pattern in Orthodox Thermodynamics, Dissolved


The four orthodox postulates surveyed in §28.3 through §28.6 — initial-condition uncertainty in classical chaos, Boltzmann's Stosszahlansatz with its supporting low-entropy initial condition, the Past Hypothesis of Albert–Loewer–Carroll, and the Thermal Time Hypothesis of Connes–Rovelli — together constitute the dominant alternative framework in contemporary foundational thermodynamics. Each is constructed to address a structural impasse the orthodox framework encounters; each preserves a cherished axiom (most often, the time-symmetry of the underlying dynamics or the unitarity of the quantum-mechanical substrate) at the cost of additional ontological commitments. The McGucken framework supplies each in single-source derived form: chaos randomness from Compton-coupled matter-tier diffusion at every event (Theorem 4); the strict Second Law from $+ic$ orientation via two independent channels (Theorem 9); the five arrows of time as parallel projections of $+ic$ orientation at every event (Theorem 11); time as the integrated coordinate of $x_4$'s active expansion, with the Connes–Rovelli modular flow recovered as the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel Wick-rotated reading (Theorems 22, 25).

The structural diagnosis is the same in each case: orthodox physics hits an impasse where the Geometric Channel and the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel both supply content the framework needs; the framework can only see one channel at a time; the missing channel is postulated by hand as new machinery; the postulate proliferates as new impasses are hit; the duality stays invisible. The McGucken framework supplies what the orthodox postulates add — without the postulates — by recognizing that the two horns of every paradox are dual readings of the same source. The four-step structural-resolution pattern of §28.1 (identify the paradoxical pair, assign channels, verify disjointness, recognize simultaneous validity) is applied in each of §28.3 through §28.6 to dissolve the specific postulate at the foundational level. The robustness property of the resulting cogenerative cascade is the subject of the following section §29.

The methodological diagnosis is Newtonian: each of the four orthodox postulates is in explicit violation of Newton's Rule I of Reasoning in Philosophy (*Principia Mathematica*, 1687, Book III): *"We are to admit no more causes of natural things than such as are both true and sufficient to explain their appearances. ... For Nature is pleased with simplicity, and affects not the pomp of superfluous causes."* The orthodox framework admits four causes (chaos initial-condition uncertainty, Stosszahlansatz with low-entropy initial condition, Past Hypothesis, Thermal Time Hypothesis) where one suffices ($dx_4/dt = ic$). The pomp of superfluous causes is dispensed with in the McGucken framework, which offers one principle, one short equation, and the chain of theorems established in the present paper as the derivation of all four content-domains the orthodox postulates address. The Heroic-Scientific-Philosophical tradition that Wheeler called for — the search for the simple foundational idea behind it all, articulated in a single short equation, with the dual structure that every paradox demands supplied from a single source — is the methodological standard the McGucken framework offers as the alternative to the orthodox postulate-accumulation pattern.


### §28.8 The 150-Year History of Hand-Waving on Time's Arrow and the Second Law: Tautologies, Shifted Terms, and the Empirical Phenomena That Demanded a Foundational Physical Mechanism


One hundred and fifty years of physics has produced an enormous body of empirical knowledge about the universe's unidirectional behavior — the cosmological expansion outward at every horizon, the radiation of stars outward through the night sky, our own aging from cradle to grave, the irreversible blackening of a grain in a photographic film when a single photon strikes it, the diffusion of inks in water observed by Brown 1827, the flow of heat from hot bodies to cold, the dissipation of sound waves, the friction of every surface in contact with every other, the dissolution of a sugar cube dropped into tea. A thousand thousand empirical results beckoned us as physicists to find the foundational causal mechanism — the underlying physical fact about the universe from which this universal unidirectional behavior descends as a derived consequence. The honest physicist's task in the face of such empirical abundance is to find the principle. Yet the published response of orthodox physics from 1865 through 2020 has been an extended pattern of circular invocations, tautological identifications, and shifted terms — each appearing at first to be progress, each on examination revealing itself to be the same prior hand-wave dressed in a new vocabulary. The pattern is consistent enough to be catalogued. The catalogue establishes nine distinct historical episodes; the structural form of each is the same: postulate the answer; identify the question with the answer; promote the postulate to a law; push the postulate to a deeper layer; replace one circular invocation with another. The McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ supplies what the 150-year history has been begging for and has not produced: the foundational causal physical mechanism from which the unidirectional empirical phenomena descend as derived theorems. The present subsection documents the hand-waving history with primary-source quotation and contrasts each move with the physical-principle resolution.


#### §28.8.1 The Empirical Demand: Why 150 Years of Observation Have Begged for a Foundational Physical Mechanism


Before cataloguing the orthodox responses, it is necessary to state plainly what the empirical record demanded — and continues to demand — of foundational physics. The unidirectional behavior of time is one of the most empirically obvious features of the universe. Every observation of the sky shows it: stars radiate outward; light arrives from increasingly distant galaxies with increasing redshift; the cosmological horizon expands. Every laboratory observation shows it: photographic film blackens when a photon strikes a grain; the blackened grain never spontaneously un-blackens. Every biological observation shows it: cells divide, organisms grow, age, and die in one direction. Every chemical observation shows it: reactions proceed toward equilibrium; products do not spontaneously revert to reactants without an external driver. Every mechanical observation shows it: friction dissipates kinetic energy into heat; the reverse process is never observed without an external work source. The empirical universe is unambiguously and overwhelmingly unidirectional at every scale of observation from the photographic grain to the cosmological horizon.

Confronted with this empirical abundance, the foundational physicist's responsibility is to identify the *causal physical mechanism* — the actual feature of reality from which the unidirectional behavior descends. The empirical signatures are the data; the foundational mechanism is the principle. To say *"entropy increases because the Second Law holds"* and *"the Second Law holds because entropy increases"* is not to explain anything; it is to identify one empirical signature with another empirical signature and to declare the identification an explanation. To say *"the universe began in a low-entropy state"* without identifying *why* it began so is not to explain anything; it is to push the empirical signature back to a temporal boundary and to declare the boundary unexplainable. To say *"irreversibility is fundamental"* and to construct operators in which the asymmetry is built in by hand is not to explain anything; it is to encode the empirical signature into the formal machinery and to call the encoding a derivation. These are the three structural shapes of the orthodox hand-wave: identification, push-back, encoding. Across nine historical episodes documented below, every orthodox response is one of these three shapes — and in many cases, two or three of them stacked.

The McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ identifies the foundational causal mechanism the empirical record has been demanding: the fourth dimension of $\mathcal{M}_G$ is actively expanding at velocity $c$ in the $+ic$ direction at every event. This is a physical fact about what the universe is doing at every event everywhere. From this physical fact the unidirectional empirical phenomena descend as derived theorems: the strict Second Law $dS/dt = (3/2)\kB/t > 0$ as Theorem 9; the five arrows of time unified as Theorem 11; Loschmidt's reversibility objection dissolved as Theorem 12; the cosmological expansion as the universe-scale projection of $+ic$ at every event; the blackening of the photographic grain as a Wick-rotation re-localization (Theorem 25) of the photon's matter-coupled position degree of freedom; the diffusion of inks as the matter-tier accumulation of inter-molecular Wick rotations (Theorem 26). The McGucken Principle supplies the foundational causal mechanism the empirical record demanded; the empirical signatures follow as derived theorems.


#### §28.8.2 The Boltzmann Foundational Hand-Wave of 1897: Postulate the Answer and Declare It Inexplicable


The Second Law was articulated by Rudolf Clausius in 1865 [Clausius1865] in the form *"Die Entropie der Welt strebt einem Maximum zu"* (the entropy of the universe tends to a maximum) — a statement that already smuggles the temporal direction into the formulation of the law itself. The "tends to" carries a unidirectional time content that cannot be derived from the time-symmetric microscopic dynamics of the era. Boltzmann's 1872 H-theorem [Boltzmann1872] proposed to derive irreversibility from time-symmetric Newtonian molecular dynamics plus the *Stosszahlansatz* (the molecular-chaos hypothesis that pre-collisional molecular velocities are uncorrelated). Loschmidt 1876 immediately identified the structural impossibility [Loschmidt1876]: time-symmetric microscopic dynamics cannot produce time-asymmetric macroscopic behavior; the Stosszahlansatz silently imports an arrow that was not present in Newton's equations (cf.\ §28.4 of the present paper for the structural diagnosis). Boltzmann acknowledged the objection and retreated to a statistical reading of the H-theorem.

By 1897, in his response to Zermelo's recurrence objection, Boltzmann articulated the foundational hand-wave that has been recycled by orthodox physics ever since:

> *"The second law of thermodynamics can be proved from the mechanical theory if one assumes that the present state of the universe, or at least that part which surrounds us, started to evolve from an improbable state and is still in a relatively improbable state. This is a reasonable assumption to make, since it enables us to explain the facts of experience, and one should not expect to be able to deduce it from anything more fundamental."*  
>   — Boltzmann, 1897 ([Boltzmann1897])

The structural form is the canonical hand-wave. Step 1: postulate the answer (the universe started in an improbable state). Step 2: justify the postulate by appeal to the empirical facts it is supposed to explain ("it enables us to explain the facts of experience"). Step 3: declare further explanation impossible ("one should not expect to be able to deduce it from anything more fundamental"). The argument is circular: the empirical fact (universal entropy increase) is invoked to justify the postulate (improbable initial state), and the postulate is then offered as the explanation of the empirical fact. The honest physicist's task — find the foundational physical mechanism — is declared impossible and replaced by a postulate justified only by the empirical record it is supposed to explain. *It is the way it is because it is*, articulated in academic prose.

The McGucken Principle does what Boltzmann declared impossible. The unidirectional behavior of entropy is deduced from something more fundamental: $dx_4/dt = ic$ with $+ic$ monotonic orientation at every event of $\mathcal{M}_G$. The strict Second Law $dS/dt = (3/2)\kB/t > 0$ is derived as Theorem 9 of the present paper from the Compton-coupling Brownian mechanism on the McGucken Sphere. Boltzmann's "one should not expect to be able to deduce it from anything more fundamental" is refuted by the deduction.


#### §28.8.3 Eddington 1927–1928: The Tautological Identification of Time's Arrow with Entropy


Arthur Eddington coins the phrase *"time's arrow"* in 1927 [Eddington1927] and, in the 1928 popular book *The Nature of the Physical World* [Eddington1928], crystallizes the canonical orthodox identification:

> *"Let us draw an arrow arbitrarily. If as we follow the arrow we find more and more of the random element in the state of the world, then the arrow is pointing towards the future; if the random element decreases the arrow points towards the past. That is the only distinction known to physics... I shall use the phrase 'time's arrow' to express this one-way property of time which has no analogue in space."*  
>   — Eddington, 1928 ([Eddington1928], Chapter IV)

Eddington concludes — following Boltzmann's statistical reading of the H-theorem — that *"time's arrow is a property of entropy alone."* This is the tautological identification in its sharpest historical form: time's arrow IS entropy increase. The identification is between two empirical signatures; the arrow is defined by the direction in which entropy increases; the arrow then points, by construction, in the direction in which entropy increases. The argument is a definition disguised as a derivation.

Arieh Ben-Naim, in his 2020 critique *Entropy and Time* ([BenNaim2020], MDPI *Entropy* **22** (4), 430), documents that this identification became the canonical statement throughout the 20th-century literature. Ben-Naim quotes Scully and Walther's *The Demon and the Quantum* writing the explicit equation form: *"entropy = time's arrow ... entropy not only explains the arrow of time, it also explains its existence; it is time."* That is not metaphorical phrasing; that is the orthodox literature genuinely identifying time with entropy at the level of an equals sign. The tautology has been promoted from observation to definition to identity.

The McGucken framework rejects the identification at its source. Time's arrow is the projection at the matter and cosmological tiers of $dx_4/dt = ic$'s $+ic$-monotonic orientation at every event. Entropy increase is a parallel projection of the same $+ic$-monotonic orientation. The two are dual readings of the same physical principle (cf.\ Theorem 11 of the present paper on the five arrows of time as parallel projections of $+ic$). Eddington's identification (time's arrow IS entropy increase) is replaced by a derivation: both are projections of $dx_4/dt = ic$, with entropy increase one specific projection among the five arrows of Theorem 11.


#### §28.8.4 Von Neumann 1932: The Recognition That Should Have Closed the 150-Year Gap — and Was Ignored


The chronological position between Eddington 1927–1928 (§28.8.3 above) and Reichenbach 1956 (§28.8.5 below) is occupied by a structural-historical observation that does not fit the canonical hand-wave pattern of §28.8.1–§28.8.3. The orthodox tradition catalogued in the present subsection §28.8 is built on hand-waves — Boltzmann's "improbable initial state" (§28.8.2), Eddington's tautological identification of time's arrow with entropy (§28.8.3) — but in 1932, John von Neumann articulated the *correct* structural recognition that should have closed the foundational-derivation gap for thermodynamics, and the orthodox community ignored it. The episode is documented here because its presence in the historical record sharpens, rather than weakens, the diagnosis of orthodox failure: the community had the right structural recognition in front of itself in 1932, with one of the most rigorous mathematical physicists of the twentieth century making it explicit, and did not follow through.

The relevant passage is in the Introduction of *Mathematische Grundlagen der Quantenmechanik* (Springer, Berlin, 1932; English translation by R.\ T.\ Beyer, *Mathematical Foundations of Quantum Mechanics*, Princeton University Press, 1955):

> *"This is not the place to point out the great success which the quantum theory attained in the period from 1900 to 1925, a development which was dominated by the names of Planck, Einstein and Bohr. At the end of this period of development, it was clear beyond doubt that all elementary processes, i.e., all occurrences of an atomic or molecular order of magnitude, obey the 'discontinuous' laws of quanta. There were also available quantitative, quantum theoretical methods in almost all directions, which for the most part yielded results in good or at least fair agreement with experiment. And, what was fundamentally of greater significance, was that the general opinion in theoretical physics had accepted the idea that the principle of continuity ('natura non facit saltus'), prevailing in the macroscopic world, is merely simulated by an averaging process in a world which in truth is discontinuous by its very nature. This simulation is such that a man generally perceives the sum of many billions of elementary processes simultaneously, so that the leveling law of large numbers completely obscures the real nature of the individual processes."*
>   — John von Neumann, *Mathematische Grundlagen der Quantenmechanik*, Springer, Berlin (1932), Introduction.


Von Neumann's passage contains four propositions that, taken together, articulate the structural identity *thermodynamics = the leveled-out perception of quantum-mechanical elementary processes*:

(VN-1) *All elementary processes — at the atomic or molecular order of magnitude — obey the discontinuous laws of quantum mechanics.* This is a categorical statement that the underlying dynamics is quantum-mechanical at every elementary event. Not "approximately quantum-mechanical in the appropriate limit"; not "quantum-mechanical with classical corrections"; categorically and at every elementary event, the dynamics is quantum-mechanical.

(VN-2) *The macroscopic principle of continuity — natura non facit saltus, the ancient axiom of classical mechanics and classical thermodynamics from Leibniz through Newton to Boltzmann — is merely simulated by an averaging process.* The continuum description of fluids in Navier-Stokes, of gases in the ideal-gas equation, of heat conduction in Fourier's law, of viscous dissipation, of the macroscopic Second Law itself — all of this continuity is, in von Neumann's diagnosis, *not foundational*. It is the appearance generated when the perceiving observer cannot resolve the underlying discontinuous events. The continuum is a *simulation*; the quantum-mechanical elementary process layer is what is real.

(VN-3) *A human observer perceives the sum of many billions of elementary processes simultaneously.* The averaging is not a calculational convenience. It is structurally forced by the temporal and spatial resolution of human perception against the elementary-process rate. The empirical thermodynamic quantities — temperature, pressure, entropy, enthalpy, free energy — are not direct readings of any single elementary process; they are *summed* readings over the $\sim 10^{43}$ elementary-process events per second per mole that occupy the perceptual window.

(VN-4) *The leveling law of large numbers completely obscures the real nature of the individual processes.* The Central Limit Theorem is the mechanism: the sum of many independent elementary events with finite variance converges in distribution to a Gaussian, and the Gaussian's shape is *invariant* under wide variation in the underlying distribution of individual events. The leveled-out signature carries *no information* about the individual processes that produced it. Von Neumann's word is "completely" — the obscuring is total at the human-perception scale.


*The structural implication.* Taking the four propositions together: classical thermodynamics — the Boltzmann–Gibbs framework, the Clausius statement of the Second Law, the empirical equations of state, the transport coefficients, the macroscopic continuum description of heat and matter — *is the leveled-out averaged signature* of $\sim 10^{43}$ quantum-mechanical elementary processes per second per mole, with the leveling so overwhelming that the underlying quantum-mechanical nature is *completely obscured* by the time the description reaches the human-perception scale.

Von Neumann published this in 1932. The recognition predates the EPR paper (1935), Jaynes 1957 (the maximum-entropy formulation of statistical mechanics, §28.7 corollary above), Connes-Rovelli 1994 (the thermal time hypothesis, §28.6), and the Linden-Popescu-Short-Winter 2009 thermalization derivation. By the chronological standard of foundational physics, the recognition that thermodynamics is the averaged-quantum has been available to the orthodox community for ninety-four years. It has not been followed through.


*Why the orthodox tradition ignored von Neumann's 1932 recognition.* Five structural reasons are documentable:

(i) *Thermodynamics predated quantum mechanics by seventy-five years.* The foundational infrastructure of statistical mechanics — Clausius 1850 ([Clausius1850]), Boltzmann 1872 ([Boltzmann1872]), Gibbs 1902 ([Gibbs1902]) — was complete before quantum mechanics existed. By 1932, the orthodox derivation chain was built on classical-Hamiltonian foundations (Liouville's theorem, the Stosszahlansatz, the ergodic hypothesis), and rebuilding it on quantum foundations would have required replacing the entire infrastructure. The community chose to *retain* the classical infrastructure and reinterpret it as the *classical limit* of an underlying quantum-statistical mechanics — a methodological choice that *preserved* the working machinery while *postponing* the structural reorientation von Neumann had identified.

(ii) *The Copenhagen cut blocked the application.* Bohr's Copenhagen interpretation, developed 1925–1927 and codified by von Neumann himself in 1932, draws a structural cut between the quantum system and the classical apparatus. Thermodynamic systems — gas containers, calorimeters, heat engines, fluid columns — sit firmly on the classical side of the cut. Treating them as quantum-mechanical at the foundational level would have violated the Copenhagen commitment that classical apparatuses are *classical*. The structural irony, sharpened by the chronological coincidence: von Neumann's *Mathematische Grundlagen* simultaneously *contains* the recognition that thermodynamics is the averaged-quantum (the introductory passage quoted above) and *codifies* the Copenhagen cut that prevents the recognition from being applied to thermodynamics. The same book did both moves in the same year.

(iii) *The "classical limit" methodology covered the gap.* Once $\hbar \to 0$ was identified as the formal classical limit, the orthodox community could treat thermodynamics as the $\hbar \to 0$ limit of quantum statistical mechanics without ever taking seriously that the underlying processes are *actually quantum*. The Ehrenfest theorem methodology — prove that quantum expectation values obey classical equations of motion in the appropriate limit, declare thermodynamics to be that limit, continue using classical statistical mechanics as the working framework — *technically* incorporates quantum mechanics but *structurally* keeps thermodynamics classical. The working calculations remained classical.

(iv) *The arrow-of-time problem became structurally harder, not easier, in quantum form.* If thermodynamics is the leveled-out average of quantum processes, then the arrow of time in thermodynamics must descend from an arrow in the quantum processes themselves. But the orthodox quantum framework, in its unitary Schrödinger formulation, has *no arrow* — the Schrödinger equation is time-symmetric, unitary evolution is reversible, the Hamiltonian is time-independent in closed systems. The orthodox community was left with a worse impasse: where does the arrow come from if the underlying quantum dynamics is time-symmetric? The arrow-insertions catalogued in §28.8.2 (Boltzmann), §28.8.3 (Eddington), §28.8.5 (Reichenbach), §28.8.6 (Prigogine), §28.8.7 (Penrose), §28.8.8 (Hawking), §28.8.9 (Albert), §28.8.10 (Carroll–Chen), and §28.8.11 (Barbour) below are easier to make at the classical statistical-mechanical level than at the quantum-statistical-mechanical level. Keeping thermodynamics classical was, in effect, a way to *localize the arrow-insertion problem* to a place where the orthodox community had practiced hand-waves for sixty years.

(v) *The Stosszahlansatz had no quantum analogue.* Boltzmann's 1872 H-theorem assumes classical molecular collisions with statistical independence of pre-collision velocities (cf.\ §28.4 of the present paper). The quantum analogue — what is the quantum-mechanical foundation for the statistical independence of pre-collision states? — was never seriously addressed. Linden-Popescu-Short-Winter 2009 is the first rigorous orthodox attempt to derive thermalization from purely unitary quantum dynamics, and even that derivation smuggles in the time-asymmetry through the initial product-state assumption. Seventy-seven years passed between von Neumann's 1932 observation and Linden-Popescu-Short-Winter's 2009 attempt to follow it through — and the attempt still inserted the arrow by hand at the initial state.


*The deeper structural irony.* Von Neumann is the one who recognized in 1932 that thermodynamics is the leveled-out average of quantum processes. He is also the one whose Hilbert-space axiomatization of quantum mechanics (with its strict unitary Schrödinger evolution and separately-postulated Born rule for measurement) made the arrow-of-time problem structurally harder. The orthodox community absorbed the *technical* content of von Neumann's QM axiomatization (Hilbert space, projection-valued measures, Born rule as primitive measurement axiom) and ignored the *structural* content of his observation about thermodynamics. Statistical mechanics continued to develop as a classical field with quantum corrections at the periphery (Bose-Einstein, Fermi-Dirac statistics for quantum gases, the Pauli paramagnetism correction); thermodynamics continued to be taught as a classical discipline; the von Neumann observation became a philosophical aside cited in foundations-of-physics seminars rather than a foundational reorientation of the field.


*The McGucken Principle as the structural completion of von Neumann's 1932 recognition.* The McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ supplies, ninety-four years later, the mechanistic content that von Neumann's 1932 observation pointed toward. Translated into McGucken terms, the four von Neumann propositions become:

(VN-1) → *All elementary processes obey the discontinuous laws of quanta.* At the matter tier, every particle is Compton-coupled to $x_4$ at the Compton frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ (Theorem 4 of the present paper), with each Compton-tick generating an isotropic random-walk displacement on the McGucken Sphere (Theorems 5–6 of the present paper). The discontinuous elementary process von Neumann identified in 1932 is the Compton-coupling tick at every event of $\mathcal{M}_G$.

(VN-2) → *Continuity is merely simulated by averaging.* The classical Navier-Stokes velocity field $\mathbf{u}(x,t)$, the classical thermodynamic state variables (temperature, pressure, entropy), the macroscopic continuum description of heat and matter are all the macroscopic *averages* of the Compton-coupled matter-tier elementary processes. The continuum is the leveled-out signature — exactly the "simulation" von Neumann named — not the foundational reality. The foundational reality is the discontinuous Compton-coupling at every event.

(VN-3) → *A human observer perceives the sum of many billions of elementary processes simultaneously.* At room temperature, a single mole of gas has $\sim 6 \times 10^{23}$ molecules; each undergoes $\sim 10^{20}$ Compton-frequency events per second (for electron-mass-scale constituents); the aggregate elementary-process rate is $\sim 10^{43}$ events per second per mole; the human perceptual resolution (milliseconds × millimeters) integrates $\sim 10^{40}$ Compton-coupled events per perception-window. The averaging is overwhelming. This is the *quantitative* version of von Neumann's "many billions of elementary processes" supplied by the McGucken framework's Compton-coupling rate.

The Gaussian is the *maximum-entropy distribution* at fixed second moment — recovering Jaynes 1957 (§28.7 corollary) as the asymptotic equilibrium reading. The CLT-leveled signature is what we observe as thermodynamic equilibrium; the "real nature of the individual processes" — the discrete Compton-tick isotropic displacements oriented at $+ic$ — is completely obscured by the leveling, exactly as von Neumann said.

The McGucken framework therefore supplies what von Neumann observed in one paragraph and the orthodox community ignored for ninety-four years: **the elementary processes are Compton-coupled $x_4$-expansion ticks at every event; the averaging is the Lindeberg–Lévy CLT applied to the matter-tier ensemble; the leveling is the diffusion that supplies both the Second Law (Theorem 9 of the present paper) and the Navier-Stokes viscous smoothing (the Clay paper [MGNavierStokes2026]). The 1932 recognition and the 2026 mechanism close together. Von Neumann saw the structural identity (thermodynamics = averaged quantum); the McGucken Principle supplies the geometric content (the elementary processes are $+ic$-oriented $x_4$-expansion at the Compton frequency at every event); the chain of theorems of the present paper derives the macroscopic thermodynamic content (Second Law of Theorem 9; five arrows of Theorem 11; Bekenstein-Hawking entropy of Theorem 15; Hawking temperature of Theorem 16; Generalized Second Law of Theorem 17; FRW cosmological thermodynamics of Theorem 18) from the elementary-process source. The ninety-four-year gap between 1932 and 2026 is the cost of the orthodox community's failure to follow through on its own deepest structural recognition.
